# Diagnostics reference

Every problem the toolchain reports has a stable code, `K` and four digits. A code keeps its meaning forever and is never reused, so you can search for it, link to it and rely on it in scripts. `k check --format json` prints the code, the span, the message and any quick fixes as one JSON object per line.

This page is generated from the compiler: the code registry, the golden test corpus in `tests/corpus`, and a fix for each code. Each example is a corpus case, shown with the output the current compiler prints for it, so the examples can't drift from the compiler. Examples are reduced test cases rather than idiomatic code, and paths such as `src/corpus/…` are the corpus's own. Some codes have no small example in the corpus; they are described in words.

## K0001–K0099: Lexer

### K0001 `unexpected-character`

**Error.** A character that cannot start any token, such as `$` or a non-ASCII letter outside a string.

Example (`tests/corpus/lexer/errors/dollar.k`):

```k,ignore
$x
```

```text
error[K0001]: unexpected character `$`
 --> src/corpus/dollar.k:1:1
  |
1 | $x
  | ^
  |
  = help: K has no `$` sigil; to pass a two-way binding, write `bind x`
```

**Fix:** Delete the character, or move it into a string or a comment. `$x` is written `bind x`.

### K0002 `unterminated-string`

**Error.** A string literal is not closed with `"` before the end of its line or file.

Example (`tests/corpus/lexer/strings/unterminated-quote-only.k`):

```k,ignore
"
```

```text
error[K0002]: unterminated string literal
 --> src/corpus/unterminated-quote-only.k:1:1
  |
1 | "
  | ^
  |
  = help: close the string with `"` before the end of the line
```

**Fix:** Close the string with `"` on the same line. Strings are single-line; use `\n` for a line break.

### K0003 `unterminated-block-comment`

**Error.** A block comment is not closed with `*/` before the end of the file.

Example (`tests/corpus/lexer/comments/block-unterminated-opener-at-eof.k`):

```k,ignore
a /*
```

```text
error[K0003]: unterminated block comment
 --> src/corpus/block-unterminated-opener-at-eof.k:1:3
  |
1 | a /*
  |   ^^
  |
  = help: close the comment with `*/`; block comments nest
```

**Fix:** Close the comment with `*/`, or use `//` line comments.

### K0004 `invalid-escape`

**Error.** A backslash escape in a string literal is not one of `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\0`, `\\`, `\"` or `\u{...}`.

Example (`tests/corpus/lexer/strings/invalid-escape-close-brace.k`):

```k,ignore
"\}"
```

```text
error[K0004]: unknown escape `\}`
 --> src/corpus/invalid-escape-close-brace.k:1:2
  |
1 | "\}"
  |  ^^
  |
  = help: the escapes are `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\0`, `\\`, `\"` and `\u{...}`
```

**Fix:** Use one of the listed escapes; write `\\` for a literal backslash.

### K0005 `invalid-color-literal`

**Error.** A color literal must be `#` followed by exactly 3, 4, 6 or 8 hexadecimal digits.

Example (`tests/corpus/lexer/colors/lone-hash.k`):

```k,ignore
#
```

```text
error[K0005]: invalid color literal `#`
 --> src/corpus/lone-hash.k:1:1
  |
1 | #
  | ^
  |
  = help: a color is `#` followed by 3, 4, 6 or 8 hexadecimal digits
```

**Fix:** Write the color as `#` and 3, 4, 6 or 8 hexadecimal digits, such as `#3B82F6`.

### K0006 `invalid-number-literal`

**Error.** A number literal is malformed, for example `0x` with no digits, a trailing `_`, or `1e` with no exponent.

Example (`tests/corpus/lexer/numbers/hex-empty.k`):

```k,ignore
0x
```

```text
error[K0006]: invalid number literal
 --> src/corpus/hex-empty.k:1:1
  |
1 | 0x
  | ^^
  |
  = help: write digits after `0x`, `0b` or `0o` that are valid for the base, and do not end a number with `_`
```

**Fix:** Complete the literal: digits after `0x`, no trailing `_`, an exponent after `e`.

### K0007 `brace-escape`

**Error.** `\{` is not an escape in K strings; write `{{` for a literal `{`.

Example (`tests/corpus/lexer/strings/brace-escape-backslash.k`):

```k,ignore
"\{"
```

```text
error[K0007]: `\{` is not an escape; use `{{`
 --> src/corpus/brace-escape-backslash.k:1:2
  |
1 | "\{"
  |  ^^
  |
  = fix: Replace `\{` with `{{`
```

**Fix:** Write `{{` for a literal `{` (the quick fix does this).

### K0008 `invalid-unicode-escape`

**Error.** A `\u{...}` escape must contain 1 to 6 hexadecimal digits naming a Unicode scalar value.

Example (`tests/corpus/lexer/strings/unicode-escape-before-quote.k`):

```k,ignore
"\u"
```

```text
error[K0008]: invalid unicode escape
 --> src/corpus/unicode-escape-before-quote.k:1:2
  |
1 | "\u"
  |  ^^
  |
  = help: write `\u{...}` with 1 to 6 hexadecimal digits naming a Unicode scalar value
```

**Fix:** Put 1 to 6 hexadecimal digits of a valid scalar value between the braces: `\u{1F44B}`.

## K0100–K0499: Parser

### K0100 `expected-token`

**Error.** The parser expected a specific token and found something else.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/declarations/config/config-missing-body.k`):

```k,ignore
config A
config B {}
```

```text
error[K0100]: expected `{`, found end of line
 --> src/corpus/config-missing-body.k:1:9
  |
1 | config A
  |         ^
```

**Fix:** Write the token the message names at the marked place; the message says what was expected and what was found.

### K0101 `unclosed-delimiter`

**Error.** An opening `(`, `[` or `{` has no matching closing delimiter.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/declarations/params/unclosed-at-eof.k`):

```k,ignore
// An unclosed parameter list reports K0101 at its `(`.
func f(x: Int
```

```text
error[K0101]: unclosed delimiter `(`
 --> src/corpus/unclosed-at-eof.k:2:7
  |
2 | func f(x: Int
  |       ^
  |
  = help: add the matching `)`
```

**Fix:** Add the matching `)`, `]` or `}`, or remove the opening one.

### K0102 `statements-on-one-line`

**Error.** Statements, members and declarations must be separated by a newline.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/declarations/errors/two-items-on-one-line.k`):

```k,ignore
// Two items on one line are K0102 at the second.
struct A {} struct B {}
```

```text
error[K0102]: expected a line break before this
 --> src/corpus/two-items-on-one-line.k:2:13
  |
2 | struct A {} struct B {}
  |             ^^^^^^
  |
  = help: statements, members and declarations each go on their own line
  = fix: Put it on its own line
```

**Fix:** Put each statement, member or declaration on its own line.

### K0103 `semicolon`

**Error.** K code does not use semicolons; statements end at the end of the line.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/declarations/errors/semicolon-after-item.k`):

```k,ignore
// A `;` after an item is K0103.
struct A {};
struct B {}
```

```text
error[K0103]: semicolons are not used in K; end the statement with a line break
 --> src/corpus/semicolon-after-item.k:2:12
  |
2 | struct A {};
  |            ^
  |
  = fix: Delete the `;`
```

**Fix:** Remove the `;`. A newline ends a statement.

### K0104 `symbolic-and`

**Error.** K writes logical conjunction as `and`, not `&&`.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/expressions/operators/symbolic-and-fix.k`):

```k,ignore
// `&&` is K0104 with a machine-applicable fix; the tree keeps `&&` as an `and`
let ok = a && b
```

```text
error[K0104]: `&&` is not an operator; write `and`
 --> src/corpus/symbolic-and-fix.k:2:12
  |
2 | let ok = a && b
  |            ^^
  |
  = fix: Replace `&&` with `and`
```

**Fix:** Write `and` instead of `&&` (machine-applicable fix).

### K0105 `symbolic-or`

**Error.** K writes logical disjunction as `or`, not `||`.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/expressions/operators/symbolic-or-fix.k`):

```k,ignore
// `||` is K0105 with a machine-applicable fix; the tree keeps `||` as an `or`
let ok = a || b
```

```text
error[K0105]: `||` is not an operator; write `or`
 --> src/corpus/symbolic-or-fix.k:2:12
  |
2 | let ok = a || b
  |            ^^
  |
  = fix: Replace `||` with `or`
```

**Fix:** Write `or` instead of `||` (machine-applicable fix).

### K0106 `symbolic-not`

**Error.** K writes logical negation as `not`, not `!`.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/expressions/operators/symbolic-not-fix.k`):

```k,ignore
// `!x` is K0106; the fix replaces `!` with `not `
let ok = !done
```

```text
error[K0106]: `!` is not an operator; write `not`
 --> src/corpus/symbolic-not-fix.k:2:10
  |
2 | let ok = !done
  |          ^
  |
  = fix: Replace `!` with `not`
```

**Fix:** Write `not` instead of `!` (machine-applicable fix).

### K0107 `ternary`

**Error.** K has no ternary operator; use an `if` expression.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/expressions/operators/ternary-with-implicit-members.k`):

```k,ignore
// `c ? .a : .b` is a ternary (K0107), not optional chaining: `? .` has a space
let tone = ok ? .success : .danger
```

```text
error[K0107]: there is no ternary operator in K
 --> src/corpus/ternary-with-implicit-members.k:2:15
  |
2 | let tone = ok ? .success : .danger
  |               ^
  |
  = help: use `if condition { a } else { b }`
```

**Fix:** Replace `a ? b : c` with `if a { b } else { c }`.

### K0108 `reserved-word`

**Error.** A reserved keyword (`as`, `is`) cannot be used as a name.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/declarations/struct/reserved-words-as-names.k`):

```k,ignore
// The reserved words `as` and `is` used as names are K0108; the parser keeps them as the name.
struct as {}
let is = 1
```

```text
error[K0108]: `as` is a reserved word and cannot be used as a name
 --> src/corpus/reserved-words-as-names.k:2:8
  |
2 | struct as {}
  |        ^^

error[K0108]: `is` is a reserved word and cannot be used as a name
 --> src/corpus/reserved-words-as-names.k:3:5
  |
3 | let is = 1
  |     ^^
```

**Fix:** Choose another name; `as` and `is` are reserved.

### K0109 `misplaced-when`

**Error.** `x when condition` is only allowed as a call argument or a list element.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/expressions/when/when-nested-in-argument-expression.k`):

```k,ignore
// `when` inside an argument's sub-expression is K0109
let a = f((x when c))
```

```text
error[K0109]: `when` is only allowed in a call argument or a list element
 --> src/corpus/when-nested-in-argument-expression.k:2:14
  |
2 | let a = f((x when c))
  |              ^^^^
  |
  = help: use `if condition { ... }` to make a value conditional
```

**Fix:** Use `x when condition` only as a call argument or a list element, such as `.class(.active when isActive)`; elsewhere write an `if`.

### K0110 `misplaced-bind`

**Error.** `bind` is only allowed directly in a call argument.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/views-styles-recovery/recovery/stray-tokens/misplaced-bind-in-view.k`):

```k,ignore
// `bind` outside an argument is K0110; the BindExpr is still built.
component T {
    view {
        text { bind name }
    }
}
```

```text
error[K0110]: `bind` is only allowed directly as a call argument
 --> src/corpus/misplaced-bind-in-view.k:4:16
  |
4 |         text { bind name }
  |                ^^^^
  |
  = help: pass the binding as an argument: `Stepper(value: bind quantity)`
```

**Fix:** Move `bind` directly into the call argument: `textField(value: bind name)`.

### K0111 `import-after-declaration`

**Error.** All imports must come before the first declaration in a file.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/declarations/imports/every-late-import-is-reported.k`):

```k,ignore
// Each import after a declaration gets its own K0111.
func main() {}
import a.B
import c.D
let x = 1
import e.F
```

```text
error[K0111]: imports must come before the first declaration
 --> src/corpus/every-late-import-is-reported.k:3:1
  |
2 | func main() {}
  | -------------- first declaration is here
3 | import a.B
  | ^^^^^^^^^^

error[K0111]: imports must come before the first declaration
 --> src/corpus/every-late-import-is-reported.k:4:1
  |
2 | func main() {}
  | -------------- first declaration is here
4 | import c.D
  | ^^^^^^^^^^

error[K0111]: imports must come before the first declaration
 --> src/corpus/every-late-import-is-reported.k:6:1
  |
2 | func main() {}
  | -------------- first declaration is here
6 | import e.F
  | ^^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Move the import above the first declaration of the file.

### K0112 `unknown-unit`

**Error.** A number literal has a suffix that is not a known unit.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/expressions/units/uppercase-base-prefix.k`):

```k,ignore
let a = 0X1F
let b = 0B101
let c = 0O17
let d = 0Xyz
```

```text
error[K0112]: `0X` is not a number prefix; write `0x`
 --> src/corpus/uppercase-base-prefix.k:1:9
  |
1 | let a = 0X1F
  |         ^^^^
  |
  = fix: Write `0x`

error[K0112]: `0B` is not a number prefix; write `0b`
 --> src/corpus/uppercase-base-prefix.k:2:9
  |
2 | let b = 0B101
  |         ^^^^^
  |
  = fix: Write `0b`

error[K0112]: `0O` is not a number prefix; write `0o`
 --> src/corpus/uppercase-base-prefix.k:3:9
  |
3 | let c = 0O17
  |         ^^^^
  |
  = fix: Write `0o`

error[K0112]: unknown unit `Xyz`
 --> src/corpus/uppercase-base-prefix.k:4:9
  |
4 | let d = 0Xyz
  |         ^^^^
  |
  = help: the units are px, em, rem, ch, vw, vh, vmin, vmax, dvh, svh, lvh, fr, %, deg, ms and s
```

**Fix:** Use a known unit suffix (`px`, `rem`, `ms`, `%`, …) or a number extension (`10.minutes`).

### K0113 `non-associative-chain`

**Error.** Comparison and range operators cannot be chained; add parentheses or split the expression.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/expressions/ranges/range-chain-is-non-associative.k`):

```k,ignore
// `a..<b..<c` is K0113
let r = 1..<2..<3
```

```text
error[K0113]: `..<` cannot be chained
 --> src/corpus/range-chain-is-non-associative.k:2:14
  |
2 | let r = 1..<2..<3
  |              ^^^
  |
  = help: add parentheses or split the expression with `and`
```

**Fix:** Add parentheses or split the comparison: `a < b and b < c`.

### K0114 `misplaced-try`

**Error.** `try` and `await` must start the expression they cover; they cannot appear to the right of a binary operator.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/expressions/operators/misplaced-await.k`):

```k,ignore
// `await` after a binary operator is K0114
let a = x * await y()
```

```text
error[K0114]: `await` must start the expression it covers
 --> src/corpus/misplaced-await.k:2:13
  |
2 | let a = x * await y()
  |             ^^^^^
  |
  = fix: Wrap the operand in parentheses
```

**Fix:** Move `try` or `await` to the start of the expression: `try await a() + b` becomes `(try await a()) + b`, or bind the result first.

### K0115 `bare-identifier-pattern`

**Error.** A bare name is not a pattern; write `let name` to bind or `.name` for an enum case.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/expressions/do-catch/catch-bare-identifier.k`):

```k,ignore
// `catch error` is K0115: bindings need `let`
func f() {
    do { try a() } catch error { }
}
```

```text
error[K0115]: a bare name is not a pattern: `error`
 --> src/corpus/catch-bare-identifier.k:3:26
  |
3 |     do { try a() } catch error { }
  |                          ^^^^^
  |
  = help: write `let name` to bind a value or `.name` to match an enum case
  = fix: Bind it: `let error`
  = fix: Match the case `.error`
```

**Fix:** Write `let name` to bind the value, or `.name` to match an enum case.

### K0116 `type-selector`

**Error.** Style blocks cannot select elements by name; give the element a class and select that.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/regressions/element-rule-does-not-cascade.k`):

```k,ignore
component T {
    style {
        button { color: red; }
        .a { color: blue; }
    }
}
```

```text
error[K0116]: style blocks cannot select elements by name: `button`
 --> src/corpus/element-rule-does-not-cascade.k:3:9
  |
3 |         button { color: red; }
  |         ^^^^^^
  |
  = help: give the element a class and select that
```

**Fix:** Give the element a class with `.class(.name)` and select `.name` in the style block.

### K0117 `missing-semicolon`

**Error.** Each style declaration except the last in a block must end with `;`.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/views-styles-recovery/styles/errors/missing-semicolons-each-reported.k`):

```k,ignore
// Every missing `;` is reported, not only the first.
component T {
    style {
        .a {
            color: red
            margin: 0
            padding: .md
        }
    }
}
```

```text
error[K0117]: expected `;` after the declaration
 --> src/corpus/missing-semicolons-each-reported.k:5:23
  |
5 |             color: red
  |                       ^
  |
  = help: every declaration except the last in its block ends with `;`
  = fix: Insert `;`

error[K0117]: expected `;` after the declaration
 --> src/corpus/missing-semicolons-each-reported.k:6:22
  |
6 |             margin: 0
  |                      ^
  |
  = help: every declaration except the last in its block ends with `;`
  = fix: Insert `;`
```

**Fix:** End the declaration with `;` (machine-applicable fix).

### K0118 `important-not-supported`

**Error.** `!important` is not supported; scoped styles make it unnecessary.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/regressions/important-without-value-has-no-fix.k`):

```k,ignore
component T {
    style {
        .a { color: !important; }
    }
}
```

```text
error[K0118]: `!important` is not supported
 --> src/corpus/important-without-value-has-no-fix.k:3:21
  |
3 |         .a { color: !important; }
  |                     ^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = help: write the value here; scoped styles make `!important` unnecessary
```

**Fix:** Remove `!important`; styles are scoped, so make the selector more specific instead.

### K0119 `invalid-range-operator`

**Error.** `..` is not an operator; use `..<` for a half-open range or `...` for a closed range.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/expressions/ranges/invalid-range-operator.k`):

```k,ignore
// `..` is K0119; the tree keeps it as a range operator
let r = 0..10
```

```text
error[K0119]: `..` is not an operator; use `..<` or `...`
 --> src/corpus/invalid-range-operator.k:2:10
  |
2 | let r = 0..10
  |          ^^
  |
  = fix: Use the half-open range `..<`
  = fix: Use the closed range `...`
```

**Fix:** Use `..<` for a half-open range or `...` for a closed one.

### K0120 `nested-optional`

**Error.** Optional types cannot be nested: `T??` is not allowed.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/declarations/types/nested-optional-at-eof.k`):

```k,ignore
let a: Int??
```

```text
error[K0120]: optional types cannot be nested
 --> src/corpus/nested-optional-at-eof.k:1:12
  |
1 | let a: Int??
  |            ^
  |
  = fix: Delete the extra `?`
```

**Fix:** Use a single `?`. To tell "missing" from "empty", use an enum.

**Error.** Annotations must come before `public`, `private` and `static`.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/regressions/annotation-order-fix-keeps-modifier-apart.k`):

```k,ignore
public@Inject let a: Int = 1
```

```text
error[K0121]: annotations must come before `public`, `private` and `static`

1 | public@Inject let a: Int = 1
```

```text
error[K0123]: expected a type, found `{`
```

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/expressions/match/missing-pattern.k`):

```text
error[K0124]: expected a pattern, found `{`
```

### K0125 `expected-declaration`

**Error.** A declaration (such as `component`, `struct` or `func`) was expected at the top level of the file.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/regressions/found-token-at-line-start-at-top-level.k`):

```k,ignore
let a = 1
}
```

```text
error[K0125]: expected a declaration, found `}`
 --> src/corpus/found-token-at-line-start-at-top-level.k:2:1
  |
2 | }
  | ^
  |
  = help: a file holds imports followed by declarations such as `component`, `struct` or `func`
```

**Fix:** Move the code into a declaration. Statements live in functions, view code in a `view` block.

### K0126 `expected-member`

**Error.** A member (a field, function, block or case) was expected in this declaration body.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/regressions/found-token-at-line-start-in-member-list.k`):

```k,ignore
component C {
    view = 1
}
```

```text
error[K0126]: expected a member, found `view`
 --> src/corpus/found-token-at-line-start-in-member-list.k:2:5
  |
2 |     view = 1
  |     ^^^^
  |
  = help: members are fields, functions, `init`, `rpc`, `case`, `use` and `view`, `style`, `loading`, `failed` or `metadata` blocks
```

**Fix:** Write a member here: a field, a function, a block (`view`, `style`, …) or a `case`.

### K0127 `duplicate-modifier`

**Error.** A modifier such as `public` or `static` is written more than once, or conflicting visibilities are combined.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/declarations/visibility/duplicate-public.k`):

```k,ignore
// Repeating a modifier is K0127 on the second one.
public public struct A {}
```

```text
error[K0127]: duplicate modifier `public`
 --> src/corpus/duplicate-public.k:2:8
  |
2 | public public struct A {}
  |        ^^^^^^
  |
  = fix: Delete the second `public`
```

**Fix:** Write each modifier once, and at most one of `public` and `private`.

### K0128 `empty-interpolation`

**Error.** An interpolation `{}` must contain an expression; write `{{` for a literal `{`.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/expressions/strings/empty-interpolation.k`):

```k,ignore
// `{}` in a string is K0128 on the two braces
let a = "x{}y"
```

```text
error[K0128]: an interpolation must contain an expression
 --> src/corpus/empty-interpolation.k:2:11
  |
2 | let a = "x{}y"
  |           ^^
  |
  = help: write `{{` for a literal `{`
  = fix: Write the braces literally
```

**Fix:** Put an expression between the braces, or write `{{` for a literal `{`.

### K0129 `throws-without-type`

**Error.** `throws` must name the error type that is thrown, for example `throws CartError`.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/declarations/protocol/rpc-throws-without-type.k`):

```k,ignore
// `throws` without a type in an rpc is K0129.
protocol P {
    rpc a() throws -> Int
    rpc b() -> Int
}
```

```text
error[K0129]: `throws` must name the error type
 --> src/corpus/rpc-throws-without-type.k:3:13
  |
3 |     rpc a() throws -> Int
  |             ^^^^^^
  |
  = help: write the thrown type, for example `throws CartError`
```

**Fix:** Name the error type: `throws CartError`.

### K0130 `multiple-enum-cases`

**Error.** Each enum case is declared with its own `case` keyword.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/regressions/enum-case-trailing-comma.k`):

```k,ignore
enum E {
    case a,
    case b
}
```

```text
error[K0130]: an enum case does not end with a comma
 --> src/corpus/enum-case-trailing-comma.k:2:11
  |
2 |     case a,
  |           ^
  |
  = fix: Remove the trailing comma
```

**Fix:** Give each case its own `case` line.

### K0131 `top-level-var`

**Error.** Top-level variables must be `let`; shared mutable state belongs in a service.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/declarations/errors/top-level-var.k`):

```k,ignore
// A top-level `var` is K0131 on `var`; it is still a FieldDecl.
var count = 0
```

```text
error[K0131]: top-level variables must be `let`
 --> src/corpus/top-level-var.k:2:1
  |
2 | var count = 0
  | ^^^
  |
  = help: shared mutable state belongs in a service
  = fix: Replace `var` with `let`
```

**Fix:** Use `let`, or move the mutable state into a service (quick fix: `let`).

### K0132 `id-selector`

**Error.** Style blocks cannot select by id; select a class instead.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/views-styles-recovery/styles/errors/id-selector-valid-hex.k`):

```k,ignore
// `#fade` is a valid color literal, so as a selector only K0132 is reported.
component T {
    style {
        .a #fade {}
    }
}
```

```text
error[K0132]: style blocks cannot select by id
 --> src/corpus/id-selector-valid-hex.k:4:12
  |
4 |         .a #fade {}
  |            ^^^^^
  |
  = help: give the element a class and select that
```

**Fix:** Give the element a class and select the class.

### K0133 `declaration-outside-rule`

**Error.** A style declaration must be inside a rule such as `.name { ... }`.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/views-styles-recovery/styles/errors/declaration-outside-rule.k`):

```k,ignore
// A declaration directly in the style block is K0133; the span covers the whole Declaration including `;`.
component T {
    style {
        color: red;
        .a { color: blue; }
    }
}
```

```text
error[K0133]: a declaration must be inside a rule
 --> src/corpus/declaration-outside-rule.k:4:9
  |
4 |         color: red;
  |         ^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = help: put it in a class rule such as `.root { ... }`
```

**Fix:** Put the declaration inside a rule such as `.name { … }`.

### K0134 `nesting-too-deep`

**Error.** Blocks, lists, expressions or style rules are nested deeper than the parser supports; the excess is skipped.

Example (`tests/corpus/parser/regressions/nesting-too-deep.k`):

```k,ignore
// Regression: nesting deeper than the parser limit (400) is K0134 once; the excess is skipped.
let a = ((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((x))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))
let b = 1
```

```text
error[K0134]: nesting exceeds the limit of 400 levels
 --> src/corpus/nesting-too-deep.k:2:410
  |
2 | let a = ((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((((x))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))))
  |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          ^
  |
  = help: split the expression or declaration into smaller parts
```

**Fix:** Flatten the code: extract part of the nesting into a function, a component or a separate rule.

## K1000–K1999: Modules, imports, name resolution, visibility, doc comments

### K1001 `stray-source-file`

**Error.** A `.k` file is outside the places the project layout allows: `App.k`, `src/<module>/` and `migrations/`.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/modules/stray-file-at-root.k`):

```k,ignore
// path: Main.k
let x = 1
```

```text
error[K1001]: this `.k` file is outside the project layout
 --> Main.k:1:1
  |
1 | // path: Main.k
  | ^
```

**Fix:** Move the file to `App.k`, to a module directory under `src/`, or to `migrations/`.

### K1002 `public-name-mismatch`

**Error.** A file's public declaration must be named like the file.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/modules/file-rule/public-name-mismatch.k`):

```k,ignore
// path: src/shop/Cart.k
public struct Basket {
    let id: Int
}
```

```text
error[K1002]: the public declaration of `Cart.k` must be named `Cart`
 --> src/shop/Cart.k:2:15
  |
2 | public struct Basket {
  |               ^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Rename the file after its public declaration, or rename the declaration.

### K1003 `multiple-public-declarations`

**Error.** A file has at most one public declaration.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/modules/file-rule/test-file-has-no-public-declaration.k`):

```k,ignore
// path: src/shop/Cart.test.k
public struct Fixture {
    let id: Int
}
```

```text
error[K1003]: a test file has no public declaration
 --> src/shop/Cart.test.k:2:15
  |
2 | public struct Fixture {
  |               ^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Move the other public declarations into files of their own, or make them module-private.

### K1004 `duplicate-declaration`

**Error.** Two declarations in one module have the same name.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/regressions/duplicate-declaration-label.k`):

```k,ignore
// K1004 has a label at the first declaration (diagnostics.md, project layout).
struct Dup {
    let v: Int
}

struct Dup {
    let w: Int
}
```

```text
error[K1004]: `Dup` is declared more than once in this module
 --> src/corpus/duplicate-declaration-label.k:6:8
  |
2 | struct Dup {
  |        --- first declared here
6 | struct Dup {
  |        ^^^
```

**Fix:** Rename one of the declarations, or delete the duplicate.

### K1005 `misplaced-declaration`

**Error.** A declaration kind appears where the layout doesn't allow it, such as `app` outside `App.k` or `migration` outside `migrations/`.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/modules/test-declaration-outside-test-file.k`):

```k,ignore
test "adds" {
    expect 1 + 1 == 2
}
```

```text
error[K1005]: tests are declared in `*.test.k` files
 --> src/corpus/test-declaration-outside-test-file.k:1:1
  |
1 | test "adds" {
  | ^^^^
```

**Fix:** Move the declaration to where its kind belongs: the `app` in `App.k`, a `migration` in `migrations/`, tests in `*.test.k` files.

### K1101 `unresolved-import`

**Error.** An import names a declaration that doesn't exist.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/names/imports/stdlib-unknown-module.k`):

```k,ignore
// A stdlib module that doesn't exist is K1101 over the whole path.
import k.tim.Clock

let count = 0
```

```text
error[K1101]: `k.tim.Clock` doesn't exist
 --> src/corpus/stdlib-unknown-module.k:2:8
  |
2 | import k.tim.Clock
  |        ^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = fix: Replace with `k.time.Clock`
```

**Fix:** Correct the module path or the name, or declare the missing declaration.

### K1102 `import-not-visible`

**Error.** An import names a declaration that isn't visible outside its module.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/modules/import-not-visible/`):

```k,ignore
// src/catalog/Helper.k
struct Helper {
    let id: Int
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/shop/Cart.k
import catalog.Helper

func describe(helper: Helper) -> Int {
    return helper.id
}
```

```text
error[K1102]: `catalog.Helper` is not public
 --> src/shop/Cart.k:1:16
  |
1 | import catalog.Helper
  |                ^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Make the declaration `public`, or import something that is.

### K1103 `import-cycle`

**Error.** Modules import each other in a cycle.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/modules/import-cycle/`):

```k,ignore
// src/a/A.k
import b.B

public struct A {
    let b: B?
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/b/B.k
import a.A

public struct B {
    let a: A?
}
```

```text
error[K1103]: this import is part of an import cycle
 --> src/a/A.k:1:8
  |
1 | import b.B
  |        ^^^

error[K1103]: this import is part of an import cycle
 --> src/b/B.k:1:8
  |
1 | import a.A
  |        ^^^
```

**Fix:** Break the cycle: move what both modules need into a third module, or invert one dependency through an interface.

### K1104 `test-only-import`

**Error.** Only test files and test-only modules may import from a `testing` module or from `k.test`.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/names/imports/production-imports-k-test.k`):

```k,ignore
// k.test is test-only: a production file importing it is K1104.
import k.test.Key

let first: Key? = nil
```

```text
error[K1104]: `k.test.Key` is test-only and can be imported only from tests
 --> src/corpus/production-imports-k-test.k:2:8
  |
2 | import k.test.Key
  |        ^^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Import test-only declarations only from `*.test.k` files and `testing` modules.

### K1105 `unused-import`

**Warning.** An import is never used.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/names/imports/name-in-comment-is-not-a-use.k`):

```k,ignore
// A name that appears only in comments and strings doesn't use the import: Clock.
import k.time.Clock

let label = "Clock"
```

```text
warning[K1105]: `k.time.Clock` is imported but never used
 --> src/corpus/name-in-comment-is-not-a-use.k:2:8
  |
2 | import k.time.Clock
  |        ^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = fix: Remove the import
```

**Fix:** Remove the import (machine-applicable fix).

### K1106 `duplicate-import`

**Error.** Two imports bring the same name into one file.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/names/imports/duplicate-of-same-declaration.k`):

```k,ignore
// Importing one declaration twice is K1106 at the second import; the fix removes that line.
import k.time.Clock
import k.time.Clock

service Stamps {
    @Inject let clock: Clock
}
```

```text
error[K1106]: `Clock` is imported twice
 --> src/corpus/duplicate-of-same-declaration.k:3:8
  |
2 | import k.time.Clock
  |        ------------ first imported here
3 | import k.time.Clock
  |        ^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = fix: Remove the duplicate import
```

**Fix:** Remove one of the imports.

### K1201 `unresolved-name`

**Error.** A name doesn't refer to any local, parameter, member or declaration in scope.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/names/unresolved-name.k`):

```k,ignore
func next(value: Int) -> Int {
    return cout + value
}
```

```text
error[K1201]: cannot find `cout` in this scope
 --> src/corpus/unresolved-name.k:2:12
  |
2 |     return cout + value
  |            ^^^^
```

**Fix:** Correct the name, or import the declaration (the quick fix imports it when exactly one visible declaration has the name).

### K1202 `unresolved-type`

**Error.** A type name doesn't refer to any visible type.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/names/unresolved-type.k`):

```k,ignore
let count: Strng = "a"
```

```text
error[K1202]: cannot find type `Strng` in this scope
 --> src/corpus/unresolved-type.k:1:12
  |
1 | let count: Strng = "a"
  |            ^^^^^
  |
  = fix: Replace with `String`
```

**Fix:** Correct the type name, or import the type (as for `K1201`).

### K1203 `unknown-member`

**Error.** A type has no member with this name.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/names/date-now-does-not-exist.k`):

```k,ignore
func stamp() -> Date {
    return Date.now
}
```

```text
error[K1203]: `Date` has no member `now`
 --> src/corpus/date-now-does-not-exist.k:2:17
  |
2 |     return Date.now
  |                 ^^^
```

**Fix:** Correct the member name; the quick fix suggests the closest member.

### K1301 `not-visible`

**Error.** A declaration or member is used where its visibility doesn't reach.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/names/private-member.k`):

```k,ignore
struct Account {
    private let secret: Int
    let name: String
}

func leak(account: Account) -> Int {
    return account.secret
}
```

```text
error[K1301]: `secret` is not visible here
 --> src/corpus/private-member.k:7:20
  |
7 |     return account.secret
  |                    ^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Use something visible at this place, or widen the declaration's visibility.

### K1302 `redundant-public-member`

**Warning.** Members are visible wherever their type is, so `public` on a member is redundant.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/names/redundant-public-member.k`):

```k,ignore
// path: src/shop/Cart.k
public struct Cart {
    public let id: Int
    let note: String
}
```

```text
warning[K1302]: members are as visible as their declaration; `public` is redundant
 --> src/shop/Cart.k:3:5
  |
3 |     public let id: Int
  |     ^^^^^^
  |
  = fix: Remove `public`
```

**Fix:** Remove `public` from the member (machine-applicable fix).

### K1303 `public-inject`

**Error.** `@Inject` fields are always private to their declaration.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/names/public-inject.k`):

```k,ignore
import k.time.Clock

service Stamps {
    @Inject public let clock: Clock
}
```

```text
error[K1303]: `@Inject` fields are always private
 --> src/corpus/public-inject.k:4:13
  |
4 |     @Inject public let clock: Clock
  |             ^^^^^^
  |
  = fix: Remove `public`
```

**Fix:** Remove `public`; injected dependencies are never API.

### K1304 `private-extend`

**Error.** An extension is `public` or visible in its module; it can't be `private`.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/names/private-extend.k`):

```k,ignore
private extend Int {
    func doubled() -> Int {
        return self * 2
    }
}
```

```text
error[K1304]: an extension can't be `private`
 --> src/corpus/private-extend.k:1:1
  |
1 | private extend Int {
  | ^^^^^^^
  |
  = fix: Remove `private`
```

**Fix:** Remove `private` from the extension.

### K1305 `conflicting-extension-member`

**Error.** Two visible extensions add a member with the same name to one type.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/names/extensions/conflicting-members-in-one-file.k`):

```k,ignore
// Two visible extensions adding one member name to one type: K1305 at the second.
extend Int {
    var dozen: Int {
        self * 12
    }
}

extend Int {
    var dozen: Int {
        self * 13
    }
}
```

```text
error[K1305]: `Int` already has a member `dozen`
 --> src/corpus/conflicting-members-in-one-file.k:9:9
  |
9 |     var dozen: Int {
  |         ^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Rename one of the members, or remove one extension from the imports.

### K1901 `unresolved-doc-link`

**Warning.** An intra-doc link names nothing that resolves.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/names/doc-links/unknown-qualified-name.k`):

```k,ignore
// A misspelled fully qualified name is K1901.

/// Maps to [`k.http.HttpStatuz`].
func statusCode() -> Int {
    return 404
}
```

```text
warning[K1901]: the doc link `k.http.HttpStatuz` doesn't resolve
 --> src/corpus/unknown-qualified-name.k:3:15
  |
3 | /// Maps to [`k.http.HttpStatuz`].
  |               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Correct the reference in backticks, import what it names, or write it fully qualified (`k.http.HttpStatus`).

## K2000–K2999: Types, expressions, effects, control flow, errors

### K2001 `type-mismatch`

**Error.** An expression's type doesn't match the type expected here.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/types/type-mismatch.k`):

```k,ignore
let count: Int = "three"
let other: Int = 3
```

```text
error[K2001]: expected `Int`, found `String`
 --> src/corpus/type-mismatch.k:1:18
  |
1 | let count: Int = "three"
  |                  ^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Convert the value, or change the expected type; the message names both types.

### K2002 `cannot-infer`

**Error.** The type of an expression can't be inferred; write it out.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/types/optionals/nil-without-expected-type.k`):

```k,ignore
// `nil` with no expected type can't be typed: K2002.
let nothing = nil
```

```text
error[K2002]: `nil` needs an optional type here
 --> src/corpus/nil-without-expected-type.k:2:15
  |
2 | let nothing = nil
  |               ^^^
```

**Fix:** Write the type out: annotate the binding (`let names: List<String> = []`) or the lambda parameter.

### K2003 `missing-argument`

**Error.** A call doesn't pass a required argument.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/ui/attributes/disabled-needs-a-value.k`):

```k,ignore
// No zero-argument flag methods: `.disabled()` misses its `Bool` (K2003).
component Pay {
    view {
        button { "Pay" }
            .disabled()
    }
}
```

```text
error[K2003]: `.disabled(…)` needs a value
 --> src/corpus/disabled-needs-a-value.k:5:23
  |
5 |             .disabled()
  |                       ^
```

**Fix:** Pass the missing argument, with its label.

### K2004 `unknown-argument-label`

**Error.** A call passes an argument label the callee doesn't declare.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/types/unknown-argument-label.k`):

```k,ignore
struct Point {
    let x: Int
    let y: Int
}

let p = Point(x: 1, z: 2, y: 3)
```

```text
error[K2004]: no parameter is labelled `z`
 --> src/corpus/unknown-argument-label.k:6:21
  |
6 | let p = Point(x: 1, z: 2, y: 3)
  |                     ^
  |
  = fix: Replace `z` with `x`
```

**Fix:** Use a label the callee declares; the quick fix suggests the closest one.

### K2005 `not-callable`

**Error.** The expression called is not a function, initializer or element.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/types/lambdas/calling-a-non-function.k`):

```k,ignore
// Calling a value that isn't a function is K2005 at the callee.
struct Point {
    let x: Int
}

func run(p: Point) -> Int {
    let n = 3
    let a = n()
    let b = p.x()
    return a + b
}
```

```text
error[K2005]: a value of `Int` can't be called
 --> src/corpus/calling-a-non-function.k:8:13
  |
8 |     let a = n()
  |             ^

error[K2005]: a value of `Int` can't be called
 --> src/corpus/calling-a-non-function.k:9:13
  |
9 |     let b = p.x()
  |             ^^^
```

**Fix:** Call a function, an initializer or an element; drop the parentheses to read a value.

### K2006 `unknown-implicit-member`

**Error.** An implicit member `.name` doesn't exist on the expected type.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/types/implicit-member-unknown.k`):

```k,ignore
enum Size {
    case small
    case large
}

let fits: Size = .small
let size: Size = .medium
```

```text
error[K2006]: `corpus.Size` has no member `medium`
 --> src/corpus/implicit-member-unknown.k:7:19
  |
7 | let size: Size = .medium
  |                   ^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Use a member the expected type has; the quick fix suggests the closest.

### K2007 `implicit-member-without-type`

**Error.** An implicit member `.name` needs an expected type to resolve against.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/types/implicit-member-without-type.k`):

```k,ignore
enum Size {
    case small
}

let size = .small
```

```text
error[K2007]: `.small` needs a type from context
 --> src/corpus/implicit-member-without-type.k:5:12
  |
5 | let size = .small
  |            ^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Write the type name (`Color.primary`), or give the binding a type.

### K2008 `missing-memberwise-field`

**Error.** A memberwise initializer omits a field that has no default value.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/types/structs/memberwise-missing-all-empty-parens.k`):

```k,ignore
// `Product()` with no arguments misses every required field: one K2008 at the gap inside `()`.
struct Product {
    let slug: String
    let price: Int
}

let empty = Product()
```

```text
error[K2008]: missing argument(s) `slug`, `price`
 --> src/corpus/memberwise-missing-all-empty-parens.k:7:21
  |
7 | let empty = Product()
  |                     ^
  |
  = fix: Insert the missing arguments
```

**Fix:** Pass the missing field, or give it a default value in the declaration.

### K2009 `unsatisfied-constraint`

**Error.** A generic argument doesn't implement the interface its `where` clause requires.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/types/collections/map-literal-key-not-hashable-inferred.k`):

```k,ignore
// When the key type is inferred from a literal, K2009 is at the key expression it came from.
let byPrice = [1.5: "cheap"]
```

```text
error[K2009]: map keys must be `Hashable`; `Double` is not
 --> src/corpus/map-literal-key-not-hashable-inferred.k:2:16
  |
2 | let byPrice = [1.5: "cheap"]
  |                ^^^
```

**Fix:** Implement the required interface on the type, or use a type that implements it.

### K2010 `missing-interface-member`

### K2405 `duplicate-storage-key`

**Error.** Two storage keys of the app have the same name, so they would read and write each other's data.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/storage/duplicate-key-name/`):

```k,ignore
// src/drafts/DraftService.k
import k.storage.LocalStorage
import k.storage.StorageKey

/// Keeps a draft across visits.
public service DraftService {
    @Inject let storage: LocalStorage

    private let draft: StorageKey<String> = StorageKey(name: "todos")
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/todos/keys.k
// Each storage key name is declared once in the app (36-local-storage.md), so two services can't
// read each other's data as their own: a second key with the same name is K2405 at its name, with a
// label at the first. Test code may reuse a name to inspect what a service stored.
import k.storage.StorageKey

/// The visitor's todos.
let savedTodos: StorageKey<List<String>> = StorageKey(name: "todos")

/// The visitor's archived todos.
let archivedTodos: StorageKey<List<String>> = StorageKey(name: "archive")
```

```k,ignore
// src/todos/keys.test.k
import k.storage.StorageKey

test Keys {
    test "a test may name an existing key" {
        let stored: StorageKey<List<String>> = StorageKey(name: "todos")
        expect stored.name == "todos"
    }
}
```

```text
error[K2405]: another storage key is named `todos`; the two would read and write each other's values
 --> src/todos/keys.k:7:61
  |
7 | let savedTodos: StorageKey<List<String>> = StorageKey(name: "todos")
  |                                                             ^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Give each storage key its own name; a test may reuse one to inspect what a service stored.

## K3000–K3999: Components, views, styles, themes, reactivity

### K3001 `annotation-mutability`

**Error.** An annotated field must be declared `let` or `var` as its annotation requires.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/config/env-field-must-be-let.k`):

```k,ignore
// `@Env` fields are `let`.
config MailConfig {
    @Env("SMTP_HOST") var host: String
}
```

```text
error[K3001]: `@Env` fields are `let`
 --> src/corpus/env-field-must-be-let.k:3:23
  |
3 |     @Env("SMTP_HOST") var host: String
  |                       ^^^
  |
  = fix: Change `var` to `let`
```

**Fix:** Use the keyword the annotation requires (the quick fix changes it): `@State`, `@Binding`, `@Form` and `@Version` are `var`; the others `let`.

### K3002 `annotation-not-allowed`

**Error.** An annotation is used on a declaration or member it doesn't apply to.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/components/annotation-not-allowed.k`):

```k,ignore
struct Settings {
    @State var volume: Int = 0
}
```

```text
error[K3002]: `@State` doesn't apply here
 --> src/corpus/annotation-not-allowed.k:2:5
  |
2 |     @State var volume: Int = 0
  |     ^^^^^^
  |
  = fix: Remove the annotation
```

**Fix:** Remove the annotation, or move it to a declaration or member it applies to.

### K3003 `missing-view`

**Error.** A component, page or layout needs a `view` block (an endpoint page has none).

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/components/missing-view.k`):

```k,ignore
component Badge {
    @Prop let label: String
}
```

```text
error[K3003]: `Badge` needs a `view` block
 --> src/corpus/missing-view.k:1:11
  |
1 | component Badge {
  |           ^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Add a `view { … }` block.

### K3004 `duplicate-block`

**Error.** A declaration has more than one `view`, `style`, `metadata`, `loading` or `failed` block.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/metadata/metadata-twice.k`):

```k,ignore
// A page has at most one `metadata` block.
page Home {
    metadata {
        title("Home")
    }

    metadata {
        description("Again")
    }

    view {
        text { "home" }
    }
}
```

```text
error[K3004]: `metadata` is declared more than once
 --> src/corpus/metadata-twice.k:7:5
  |
3 |     metadata {
  |     -------- first declared here
7 |     metadata {
  |     ^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Merge the blocks into one.

### K3005 `invalid-annotated-type`

**Error.** A `@Slot`, `@Stylable` or `@Emits` field's type doesn't fit its annotation (`View`, `Classes`, `Event<T>`).

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/ui/stylable/stylable-type-must-be-classes.k`):

```k,ignore
// A `@Stylable` prop is a class hook: its type is `Classes` (K3005 otherwise).
component Chip {
    @Stylable let container: String

    view {
        text { "chip" }
    }
}
```

```text
error[K3005]: a `@Stylable` field is `Classes`
 --> src/corpus/stylable-type-must-be-classes.k:3:30
  |
3 |     @Stylable let container: String
  |                              ^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Use the type the annotation needs: `View` for `@Slot`, `Classes` for `@Stylable`, `Event<T>` for `@Emits`.

### K3010 `write-to-derived`

**Error.** A `@Derived` value is computed and can't be assigned.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/components/write-to-derived.k`):

```k,ignore
component Total {
    @State var count: Int = 0
    @Derived let doubled: Int = count * 2

    func reset() {
        count = 0
        doubled = 0
    }

    view {
        text { "{doubled}" }
    }
}
```

```text
error[K3010]: `doubled` is `@Derived`: it is computed, never assigned
 --> src/corpus/write-to-derived.k:7:9
  |
3 |     @Derived let doubled: Int = count * 2
  |                  ------- declared `@Derived` here
7 |         doubled = 0
  |         ^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Make the value `@State` if it is set directly, or change the inputs the `@Derived` value is computed from.

### K3011 `state-write-in-derived`

**Error.** A `@Derived` initializer can't write state.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/ui/reactivity/state-write-in-derived.k`):

```k,ignore
// Writing `@State` while computing a `@Derived` value is K3011 at the assignment
// (03-reactivity.md).
component Total {
    @State var count: Int = 0
    @State var reads: Int = 0
    @Derived let label: String = if count > 0 {
        reads += 1
        "some"
    } else {
        "none"
    }

    view {
        text { label }
    }
}
```

```text
error[K3011]: a `@Derived` value can't write state while it is computed
 --> src/corpus/state-write-in-derived.k:7:9
  |
7 |         reads += 1
  |         ^^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Move the write into a function or an `@Effect`.

### K3012 `throwing-effect-or-handler`

**Error.** `@Effect` functions and event handlers handle their own errors, so they can't be `throws`.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/components/effect-throws.k`):

```k,ignore
enum SyncError implements Error {
    case failed
}

component Sync {
    @Effect(on: [])
    func start() throws SyncError {
    }

    view {
        text { "syncing" }
    }
}
```

```text
error[K3012]: an `@Effect` can't throw: nothing could catch its error
 --> src/corpus/effect-throws.k:7:18
  |
7 |     func start() throws SyncError {
  |                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Remove `throws` and handle the errors inside, usually by recording them in state (the quick fix wraps the body in `do`/`catch`).

### K3013 `discarded-timer-handle`

**Warning.** The `TimerHandle` returned by `clock.every` or `clock.after` in an effect is discarded, so the timer outlives the component.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/components/discarded-timer-handle.k`):

```k,ignore
import k.time.Clock

component Ticker {
    @Inject let clock: Clock
    @State var ticks: Int = 0

    @Effect(on: [])
    func start() {
        clock.every(1.second) { ticks += 1 }
    }

    @Effect(on: [])
    func startAndStop() {
        let timer = clock.every(1.second) { ticks += 1 }

        onCleanup { timer.cancel() }
    }

    view {
        text { "{ticks}" }
    }
}
```

```text
warning[K3013]: the timer is never cancelled: keep its `TimerHandle` and cancel it in `onCleanup`
 --> src/corpus/discarded-timer-handle.k:9:9
  |
9 |         clock.every(1.second) { ticks += 1 }
  |         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = fix: Bind the handle and cancel it in `onCleanup`
```

**Fix:** Keep the handle and cancel it in `onCleanup { timer.cancel() }`.

### K3014 `write-to-prop`

**Error.** A component writes to its own `@Prop`, a one-way input; make it a `@Binding`.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/ui/props/compound-write-to-prop.k`):

```k,ignore
// Compound assignment to a prop is a write too (K3014 at the place).
component Counter {
    @Prop let count: Int

    func increment() {
        count += 1
    }

    view {
        text { "{count}" }
    }
}
```

```text
error[K3014]: `count` is a `@Prop`: the parent owns it
 --> src/corpus/compound-write-to-prop.k:6:9
  |
3 |     @Prop let count: Int
  |               ----- declared `@Prop` here
6 |         count += 1
  |         ^^^^^
  |
  = fix: Change `@Prop let` to `@Binding var`
```

**Fix:** Make the field a `@Binding` so the parent sees the change, or keep a local `@State` copy.

### K3015 `not-bindable`

**Error.** `bind` needs a `@State`, `@Binding` or `@Form` place, or a field of one.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/ui/bindings/bind-literal.k`):

```k,ignore
// Literals and other non-places can't be bound.
component Stepper {
    @Binding var value: Int

    view {
        text { "{value}" }
    }
}

component Cart {
    @State var quantity: Int = 1

    view {
        Stepper(value: bind 5)
        Stepper(value: bind quantity + 1)
    }
}
```

```text
error[K3015]: only `@State`, `@Binding` and `@Form` values (and paths into them) can be bound
  --> src/corpus/bind-literal.k:14:29
   |
14 |         Stepper(value: bind 5)
   |                             ^

error[K3015]: only `@State`, `@Binding` and `@Form` values (and paths into them) can be bound
  --> src/corpus/bind-literal.k:15:29
   |
15 |         Stepper(value: bind quantity + 1)
   |                             ^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Bind a `@State`, `@Binding` or `@Form` value, or a field of one.

### K3016 `missing-bind`

**Error.** A value passed to a `@Binding` prop or a `Binding` argument needs `bind`.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/ui/bindings/missing-bind-on-input.k`):

```k,ignore
// Inputs take a `Binding<T>` too: `textField(value: name)` misses `bind` (K3016).
component Signup {
    @State var name: String = ""
    @State var agreed: Bool = false

    view {
        textField(value: name)
        checkbox(isChecked: bind agreed)
    }
}
```

```text
error[K3016]: a two-way binding is passed with `bind`
 --> src/corpus/missing-bind-on-input.k:7:26
  |
7 |         textField(value: name)
  |                          ^^^^
  |
  = fix: Insert `bind `
```

**Fix:** Write `bind` before the value (machine-applicable fix).

### K3017 `throwing-handler`

**Error.** A function passed to `.on(…)` is `throws`; handlers handle their own errors.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/ui/events/throwing-async-handler-function.k`):

```k,ignore
// An `async throws` function is not a handler either (K3017).
enum SaveError implements Error {
    case failed
}

component Editor {
    func save() async throws SaveError {
        throw .failed
    }

    view {
        button { "Save" }
            .on(click: save)
    }
}
```

```text
error[K3017]: an event handler can't throw: nothing could catch its error
  --> src/corpus/throwing-async-handler-function.k:13:24
   |
13 |             .on(click: save)
   |                        ^^^^
```

**Fix:** Pass a function that handles its own errors, or wrap the call in `do`/`catch`.

### K3018 `unexpected-bind`

**Error.** `bind` is passed where no binding is expected.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/ui/bindings/bind-to-plain-prop.k`):

```k,ignore
// `bind` where no binding is expected (a `@Prop`, or an element argument that
// isn't a `Binding`) is K3018 with a fix that removes `bind `.
component Label {
    @Prop let text: String

    view {
        paragraph { text }
    }
}

component Home {
    @State var title: String = ""

    view {
        Label(text: bind title)
        image(source: Url("https://k.dev/a.png"), description: bind title)
    }
}
```

```text
error[K3018]: `bind` is only for `@Binding` props and `Binding` arguments
  --> src/corpus/bind-to-plain-prop.k:15:21
   |
15 |         Label(text: bind title)
   |                     ^^^^^
   |
   = fix: Remove `bind `

error[K3018]: `bind` is only for `@Binding` props and `Binding` arguments
  --> src/corpus/bind-to-plain-prop.k:16:64
   |
16 |         image(source: Url("https://k.dev/a.png"), description: bind title)
   |                                                                ^^^^^
   |
   = fix: Remove `bind `
```

**Fix:** Remove `bind` and pass the value.

### K3020 `load-cycle`

**Error.** `@Load` initializers depend on each other in a cycle.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/load/load-reads-itself.k`):

```k,ignore
// A load that reads its own field is a cycle of one.
func next(value: Int) async -> Int {
    return value + 1
}

page Loop {
    @Load let a: Int = await next(value: a)

    view {
        text { "{a}" }
    }

    loading {
    }
}
```

```text
error[K3020]: the `@Load` field `a` waits for itself through a cycle of loads
 --> src/corpus/load-reads-itself.k:7:15
  |
7 |     @Load let a: Int = await next(value: a)
  |               ^
```

**Fix:** Break the cycle: load one value from the other's inputs instead of from the other value.

### K3021 `load-not-codable`

**Error.** A `@Load` value must be `Codable`, because server-rendered data is sent to the browser.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/load/load-secret.k`):

```k,ignore
// `Secret<T>` isn't `Codable`, so it can't be loaded.
func token() async -> Secret<String> {
    return Secret("x")
}

page Token {
    @Load let token: Secret<String> = await token()

    view {
        text { "token" }
    }

    loading {
    }
}
```

```text
error[K3021]: `@Load` values are sent to the browser, so they are `Codable`; `Secret<String>` isn't
 --> src/corpus/load-secret.k:7:22
  |
7 |     @Load let token: Secret<String> = await token()
  |                      ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Make the loaded type `Codable`, or load a `Codable` summary of it.

### K3022 `missing-loading-block`

**Error.** A declaration with `@Load` fields needs a `loading` block.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/components/load-needs-loading-block.k`):

```k,ignore
    return 1
}

page Stats {
    @Load let total: Int = await count()

    view {
        text { "{total}" }
    }
}
```

```text
 --> src/corpus/load-needs-loading-block.k:5:6
  |
5 | page Stats {
  |      ^^^^^
  |
  = fix: Add an empty `loading { }`
```

**Fix:** Add a `loading { … }` block.

### K3023 `reserved-reload`

**Error.** A declaration with `@Load` fields has a generated `reload()`, so it can't declare a member named `reload`.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/load/reload-is-reserved.k`):

```k,ignore
// Declaring a member named `reload` next to `@Load` fields is an error; without them it's an ordinary
// name.
func count() async -> Int {
    return 1
}

page Stats {
    @Load let total: Int = await count()

    func reload() {
    }

    view {
        text { "{total}" }
    }

    loading {
    }
}

page Plain {
    func reload() {
    }

    view {
        button { "Reload" }
            .on(click: reload)
    }
}
```

```text
error[K3023]: `reload` is generated for declarations with `@Load` fields
  --> src/corpus/reload-is-reserved.k:10:10
   |
10 |     func reload() {
   |          ^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Rename the member; `reload()` is generated.

### K3024 `load-error-not-codable`

**Error.** The errors a `@Load` initializer can throw must be `Codable`, because a server-rendered `failed` is hydrated.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/load/load-error-not-codable.k`):

```k,ignore
// The errors a load can throw are serialized for `failed` too, so they are `Codable`.
enum FetchError implements Error {
    case offline
}

func fetch() async throws FetchError -> Int {
    return 1
}

page Stats {
    @Load let total: Int = try await fetch()

    view {
        text { "{total}" }
    }

    loading {
    }
}
```

```text
error[K3024]: a load's error is sent to `failed`, so it is `Codable`; `corpus.FetchError` isn't
  --> src/corpus/load-error-not-codable.k:11:28
   |
11 |     @Load let total: Int = try await fetch()
   |                            ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Make the error type `Codable`, or map the error to a `Codable` one inside the initializer.

### K3025 `status-outside-failed`

**Error.** `status(_:)` is allowed only in a `metadata` block inside `failed`.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/metadata/status-in-page-metadata.k`):

```k,ignore
// `status(_:)` is allowed only inside `failed`, so the page-level block can't set it.
page Missing {
    metadata {
        title("Missing")
        status(.notFound)
    }

    view {
        text { "missing" }
    }
}
```

```text
error[K3025]: `status(_:)` is set in a `metadata` block inside `failed`
 --> src/corpus/status-in-page-metadata.k:5:9
  |
5 |         status(.notFound)
  |         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Move `status(_:)` into a `metadata` block inside `failed`.

### K3026 `derived-cycle`

**Error.** A `@Derived` field's initializer reads the field itself, directly or through other `@Derived` fields.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/ui/reactivity/derived-cycle-through-untracked.k`):

```k,ignore
// `untracked { … }` reads without subscribing, but the value is still
// needed to compute the field: a cycle through it is K3026 as well.
component Tracker {
    @Derived let first: Int = untracked { second } + 1
    @Derived let second: Int = first * 2

    view {
        text { "{first}" }
    }
}
```

```text
error[K3026]: the `@Derived` field `first` depends on itself through a cycle of `@Derived` fields
 --> src/corpus/derived-cycle-through-untracked.k:4:18
  |
4 |     @Derived let first: Int = untracked { second } + 1
  |                  ^^^^^

error[K3026]: the `@Derived` field `second` depends on itself through a cycle of `@Derived` fields
 --> src/corpus/derived-cycle-through-untracked.k:5:18
  |
5 |     @Derived let second: Int = first * 2
  |                  ^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Compute the value from inputs that don't depend on it.

### K3027 `page-without-title`

**Warning.** A view page has no `title`: neither its `metadata`, nor its layout's, nor the app's sets one.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/metadata/page-without-title/`):

```k,ignore
// App.k
// The app's metadata sets no title, so a page without one of its own, or
// from its layout, is K3027 (22-metadata.md, "Rules").
import site.Plain

@Layout(Plain)
public app Site {
    metadata {
        locale(.english)
    }
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/site/Pages.k
import k.http.HttpResponse
import k.http.IncomingRequest

// No metadata at all, under the app's default layout: K3027, and the fix
// adds a `metadata` block.
page Home at "/" {
    view {
        text { "Home" }
    }
}

// A metadata block without a title: K3027, and the fix adds the title to it.
page OrderHistory {
    metadata {
        description("Your orders")
    }

    view {
        text { "Orders" }
    }
}

// Its own title: nothing.
page About {
    metadata {
        title("About us")
    }

    view {
        text { "About" }
    }
}

// The title comes from its layout: nothing.
@Layout(Shop)
page Catalog {
    view {
        text { "Catalog" }
    }
}

// Out of every layout, with no title: K3027.
@NoLayout
page Bare {
    view {
        text { "Bare" }
    }
}

// A title only inside `failed` is the failure's, not the page's: K3027.
page Product {
    @Load let name: String = try await fetchName()

    view {
        text { name }
    }

    loading {
        text { "…" }
    }

    failed(let error) {
        metadata {
            title("Not found")
        }

        text { "Missing" }
    }
}

// An endpoint page has no metadata: nothing.
page Ping at "/ping" {
    @Get
    func run(request: IncomingRequest) async -> HttpResponse {
        return HttpResponse(status: .ok)
    }
}

func fetchName() async throws LoadError -> String {
    return "x"
}

enum LoadError implements Error, Codable {
    case missing
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/site/Plain.k
/// The default layout: no title of its own.
public layout Plain {
    @Slot let content: View

    view {
        content
    }
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/site/Shop.k
/// A layout with a default title for its pages.
public layout Shop {
    @Slot let content: View

    metadata {
        title("Acme Shop")
    }

    view {
        content
    }
}
```

```text
warning[K3027]: the page `Home` has no `title`
 --> src/site/Pages.k:6:6
  |
6 | page Home at "/" {
  |      ^^^^
  |
  = note: neither its `metadata`, nor its layout's, nor the app's sets one
  = fix: Add `title("Home")`

warning[K3027]: the page `OrderHistory` has no `title`
  --> src/site/Pages.k:13:6
   |
13 | page OrderHistory {
   |      ^^^^^^^^^^^^
   |
   = note: neither its `metadata`, nor its layout's, nor the app's sets one
   = fix: Add `title("Order history")`

warning[K3027]: the page `Bare` has no `title`
  --> src/site/Pages.k:44:6
   |
44 | page Bare {
   |      ^^^^
   |
   = note: neither its `metadata`, nor its layout's, nor the app's sets one
   = fix: Add `title("Bare")`

warning[K3027]: the page `Product` has no `title`
  --> src/site/Pages.k:51:6
   |
51 | page Product {
   |      ^^^^^^^
   |
   = note: neither its `metadata`, nor its layout's, nor the app's sets one
   = fix: Add `title("Product")`
```

**Fix:** Add `title("…")` to the page's `metadata` block (the quick fix does this), or give its layout or the app a default `title`.

### K3028 `long-description`

### K3105 `unknown-event`

**Error.** `.on(name:)` names an event the element or component doesn't fire.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/ui/events/prop-is-not-an-event.k`):

```k,ignore
// Only `@Emits` fields are events: `.on(label: …)` on a component whose `label`
// is a prop is K3105.
component Counter {
    @Prop let label: String = "Count"

    view {
        text { label }
    }
}

component Home {
    @State var count: Int = 0

    view {
        Counter()
            .on(label: { count += 1 })
    }
}
```

```text
error[K3105]: `corpus.Counter` has no event `label`: it fires no events
  --> src/corpus/prop-is-not-an-event.k:16:17
   |
16 |             .on(label: { count += 1 })
   |                 ^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Use an event the element or component declares with `@Emits`.

### K3106 `missing-for-key`

**Error.** A `for` loop in a view needs a `key`.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/ui/for-key/missing-key-without-id.k`):

```k,ignore
// Without an `id` on the item type there is nothing to suggest.
component Names {
    @Prop let names: List<String>

    view {
        for name in names {
            text { name }
        }
    }
}
```

```text
 --> src/corpus/missing-key-without-id.k:6:26

6 |         for name in names {
  |                          ^
```

**Fix:** Add a key: `for item in items key item.id`.

## K4000–K4999: Services, dependency injection, layering, server/client boundary

### K4001 `missing-implementation`

**Error.** An injected interface has no implementation.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/di/missing-implementation.k`):

```k,ignore
interface Payments {
    func charge(cents: Int) async
}

service Checkout {
    @Inject let payments: Payments
}
```

```text
error[K4001]: no service implements `corpus.Payments`
 --> src/corpus/missing-implementation.k:6:27
  |
6 |     @Inject let payments: Payments
  |                           ^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Declare a service that implements the interface, or bind one with `use` in `App.k`.

### K4002 `ambiguous-implementation`

**Error.** An injected interface has several implementations and no `use` rule picks one.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/services/ambiguous-implementation/`):

```k,ignore
// App.k
// Two implementations and no `use` rule: the injection is ambiguous.
public app Shop {}
```

```k,ignore
// src/pay/FakePayments.k
// Another implementation.
public service FakePayments implements PaymentProvider {
    func charge(cents: Int) async {
    }
}
```

### K4003 `dependency-cycle`

**Error.** Injected services depend on each other in a cycle.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/services/self-injection.k`):

```k,ignore
// A service that injects itself is a cycle of one.
service Loop {
    @Inject let again: Loop
}
```

```text
error[K4003]: `corpus.Loop` injects itself
 --> src/corpus/self-injection.k:3:24
  |
3 |     @Inject let again: Loop
  |                        ^^^^
```

**Fix:** Break the cycle: extract what both need into a third service, or pass a value instead of injecting.

### K4004 `scope-violation`

**Error.** A service injects a service with a shorter scope, or a `.server` service or job reaches request state.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/di/server-scope-injects-session.k`):

```k,ignore
import k.auth.Session

@Scope(.server)
service Cache {
    @Inject let session: Session
}
```

```text
error[K4004]: a `.server` service can't inject `k.auth.Session`, which is `.app` and may end sooner
 --> src/corpus/server-scope-injects-session.k:5:26
  |
5 |     @Inject let session: Session
  |                          ^^^^^^^
  |
  = note: corpus.Cache → k.auth.Session
```

**Fix:** Inject only services with the same or a longer scope; pass request data as arguments instead.

### K4005 `layering-violation`

**Error.** A declaration injects something its kind may not inject (components never inject protocols).

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/services/layering/component-injects-database.k`):

```k,ignore
// `Database` is injectable only into server-side services.
import k.db.Database

component Health {
    @Inject let database: Database

    view {
        text { "health" }
    }
}
```

```text
error[K4005]: a component can't inject server infrastructure
 --> src/corpus/component-injects-database.k:5:27
  |
5 |     @Inject let database: Database
  |                           ^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Inject what the declaration's layer allows; a component injects a client-side service that wraps the protocol.

### K4006 `foreign-state-write`

**Error.** Only a service's own methods can write its fields.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/services/state-plain-var-field.k`):

```k,ignore
// The rule covers plain `var` fields, not only `@State`.
service Retry {
    var attempts: Int = 0
}

component RetryButton {
    @Inject let retry: Retry

    func clear() {
        retry.attempts = 0
    }

    view {
        button { "Clear" }
            .on(click: clear)
    }
}
```

```text
error[K4006]: only `Retry`'s own methods write its field `attempts`
  --> src/corpus/state-plain-var-field.k:10:9
   |
 3 |     var attempts: Int = 0
   |         -------- declared here
10 |         retry.attempts = 0
   |         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Add a method to the service that makes the change, and call it.

### K4007 `server-only-in-client`

**Error.** A server-only declaration is used by code that reaches the browser.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/config/secret-in-client-code.k`):

```k,ignore

component Pay {
    @Prop let key: Secret<String>

    view {
        text { "pay" }
    }
}
```

```text
error[K4007]: `Secret` is server-only and can't be used in code that reaches the browser
 --> src/corpus/secret-in-client-code.k:3:20
  |
3 |     @Prop let key: Secret<String>
  |                    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Move the code to the server side, or reach the server through a protocol.

### K4008 `service-on-both-sides`

**Error.** A service is server-only and client-only at once.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/boundary/service-on-both-sides.k`):

```text
  --> src/corpus/service-on-both-sides.k:10:9

10 | service Sync {

```

**Fix:** Remove the dependency that makes the service one-sided, or split it into two services.

### K4009 `job-reaches-session`

**Error.** A job's dependency graph reaches `Session` or `SessionManager`.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/jobs/job-reaches-session.k`):

```k,ignore
// A job has no session (30-background-jobs.md): a job whose dependency graph
// reaches `Session` is K4009 at the job's name, with a note naming the path,
// directly or through another service.
import k.auth.Session
import k.server.Job
import k.server.JobError

struct Mail implements Codable {
    let to: String
}

    @Inject let session: Session
}

service MailJob implements Job<Mail> {

    func run(payload: Mail) async throws JobError {
    }
}

service DirectJob implements Job<Mail> {
    @Inject let session: Session

    func run(payload: Mail) async throws JobError {
    }
}

service FineJob implements Job<Mail> {
    func run(payload: Mail) async throws JobError {
    }
}
```

```text
error[K4009]: the job `MailJob` reaches `Session`, but a job runs without a session
  --> src/corpus/job-reaches-session.k:16:9

16 | service MailJob implements Job<Mail> {
   |         ^^^^^^^
   |
   = note: corpus.MailJob → corpus.Audit → k.auth.Session

error[K4009]: the job `DirectJob` reaches `Session`, but a job runs without a session
  --> src/corpus/job-reaches-session.k:23:9
   |
23 | service DirectJob implements Job<Mail> {
   |         ^^^^^^^^^
   |
   = note: corpus.DirectJob → k.auth.Session
```

**Error.** In `use X for Y`, `X` must be `Y` or implement it.

### K4011 `use-expression-not-allowed`

### K4012 `client-only-during-ssr`

**Error.** A client-only interface is called from code that can run during server rendering.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/boundary/client-only-call-during-ssr.k`):

```k,ignore
// A client-only interface can't be called from code that may run during server rendering, such as a

let draftKey: StorageKey<String> = StorageKey(name: "draft")
```

```text
11 |     let cleared: Void = storage.remove(key: draftKey)
   |                         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

### K4026 `remote-client-not-a-protocol`

**Error.** `RemoteClient.at` builds a client of a protocol: use it where a protocol type is expected.

```k,ignore
// `RemoteClient.at` builds a client of the protocol its result is used as
// (40-workspaces-and-services.md); the result must be a protocol.
import k.rpc.RemoteClient
import k.rpc.RpcOnlyError

protocol MerchantEvents {
    rpc paid(chargeId: String) throws RpcOnlyError
}

struct Hook {
    let url: Url
}

@Scope(.server)
service Notifier {
//      ^^^^^^^^ side: server-only
    func notify(url: Url, token: Secret<String>) async throws RpcOnlyError {
        let events: MerchantEvents = RemoteClient.at(url: url, token: token)
        //                           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ type: corpus.MerchantEvents
        try await events.paid(chargeId: "ch_1")
        let quick: MerchantEvents = RemoteClient.at(url: url, token: token, timeout: 2.seconds)
        try await quick.paid(chargeId: "ch_2")
    }

    func wrong(url: Url, token: Secret<String>) {
        let hook: Hook = RemoteClient.at(url: url, token: token)
        let unknown = RemoteClient.at(url: url, token: token)
    }
}
```

```text
error[K4026]: `RemoteClient.at` builds a client of a protocol, and `corpus.Hook` is not one
  --> src/corpus/remote-client-at.k:26:39
   |
26 |         let hook: Hook = RemoteClient.at(url: url, token: token)
   |                                       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Give the binding a protocol type: `let events: PaymentEvents = RemoteClient.at(…)`.

```k,ignore
enum Filter {

}

page Map {
    @Param let tags: List<String>

    @Param let since: Date

}
```

```text
   |                        ^^^^^

```

### K5003 `at-template-mismatch`

**Error.** An `at` template and the page's path `@Param` fields don't match one to one.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/pages/at/template-repeats-param.k`):

```text
2 | page Product at "/p/{id}/{id}" {
  |                          ^^^^
```

**Fix:** Name every path parameter once in the template, as `{name}`, and declare a `@Param` for each.

### K5004 `endpoint-without-at`

**Error.** An endpoint page needs an `at` clause.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/pages/endpoints/endpoint-without-at.k`):

### K5006 `not-a-guard`

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/protocols/protocol-requires-not-a-guard.k`):

```k,ignore
    rpc ping() throws RpcOnlyError
}

```

### K5007 `missing-sign-in-page`

### K5009 `layout-on-endpoint`

### K5011 `duplicate-handler-method`

```text
21 |     func replace(body: IncomingRequest) async -> HttpResponse {

error[K5012]: a handler is `func name(request: IncomingRequest) async -> HttpResponse`
  --> src/corpus/handler-signature.k:26:10
   |

   |          ^^^^^^

error[K5012]: a handler is `func name(request: IncomingRequest) async -> HttpResponse`
```

### K5013 `set-cookie-header`

**Error.** A response sets a literal `set-cookie` header; cookies are set only through `Session`.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/pages/endpoints/set-cookie-header.k`):

```k,ignore
// Cookies are set only through `Session` (27-endpoint-pages.md): a literal
// `set-cookie` header name, in any case, is K5013 at the key. Other headers
// and a computed name (which panics at run time instead) are not.
import k.http.HttpResponse
import k.http.IncomingRequest

page Hook at "/hook" {
    @Post
    func run(request: IncomingRequest) async -> HttpResponse {
        let name = request.headers["x-name"] ?? "x-other"
        let other = HttpResponse(status: .ok).headers([name: "a=b", "cache-control": "no-store"])

        return HttpResponse(status: .ok)
            .headers(["set-cookie": "id=1", "x-trace": "abc"])
            .headers(["Set-Cookie": "id=2"])
    }
}
```

```text
error[K5013]: a response can't set `set-cookie`: cookies are set only through `Session`
  --> src/corpus/set-cookie-header.k:14:23
   |
14 |             .headers(["set-cookie": "id=1", "x-trace": "abc"])
   |                       ^^^^^^^^^^^^
   |
   = help: sign the user in or out with `SessionManager`, which sets the session cookie

error[K5013]: a response can't set `set-cookie`: cookies are set only through `Session`
  --> src/corpus/set-cookie-header.k:15:23
   |
15 |             .headers(["Set-Cookie": "id=2"])
   |                       ^^^^^^^^^^^^
   |
   = help: sign the user in or out with `SessionManager`, which sets the session cookie
```

**Fix:** Set the cookie through `Session` (`SessionManager`), never as a raw `set-cookie` header.

### K5014 `guard-on-layout`

**Error.** A layout has a `requires` clause, which the server never checks: guards go on the pages.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/pages/layouts/guard-on-layout.k`):

```k,ignore
// The server checks the guards of the page it answers, never of its layout, so a `requires` clause
// on a layout is K5014, whatever it names. A page's own clause is fine.
import k.auth.RateLimit

layout Shop requires RateLimit(10.perMinute) {
    @Slot let content: View

    view {
        content
    }
}

layout Plain requires Missing {
    @Slot let content: View

    view {
        content
    }
}

@Layout(Shop)
page Home requires RateLimit(10.perMinute) {
    view {
        text { "home" }
    }
}
```
