```text
error[K5014]: the server never checks a layout's `requires` clause
 --> src/corpus/guard-on-layout.k:5:13
  |
5 | layout Shop requires RateLimit(10.perMinute) {
  |             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = help: the server checks the guards of the page it answers: put the clause on each page that renders in `Shop`

error[K5014]: the server never checks a layout's `requires` clause
  --> src/corpus/guard-on-layout.k:13:14
   |
13 | layout Plain requires Missing {
   |              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
   |
   = help: the server checks the guards of the page it answers: put the clause on each page that renders in `Plain`
```

**Fix:** Move the clause to each page that renders in the layout: `page Dashboard requires Authenticated`.

## K5500–K5999: Protocols and RPC

### K5501 `rpc-without-throws`

**Error.** Every `rpc` declares `throws`: an error enum with a `rpcFailure(RpcFailure)` case, or `RpcOnlyError`.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/rpc/rpc-without-throws.k`):

```k,ignore
import k.rpc.RpcOnlyError

protocol Store {
    rpc products() -> List<Int>
    rpc count() throws RpcOnlyError -> Int
}
```

```text
error[K5501]: rpc `products` must declare `throws`: every remote call can fail
 --> src/corpus/rpc-without-throws.k:4:9
  |
4 |     rpc products() -> List<Int>
  |         ^^^^^^^^
  |
  = fix: Add `throws RpcOnlyError`
```

**Fix:** Add `throws RpcOnlyError`, or an error enum with a `case rpcFailure(RpcFailure)` (the quick fix adds `throws RpcOnlyError`).

### K5502 `rpc-error-without-failure-case`

**Error.** An rpc's error enum needs exactly one `rpcFailure(RpcFailure)` case.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/protocols/failure-case-with-wrong-payload.k`):

```k,ignore
// The `rpcFailure` case carries an `RpcFailure`, nothing else.
enum CartError implements Error, Codable {
    case rpcFailure(String)
}

protocol Store {
    rpc add() throws CartError -> Int
}
```

```text
error[K5502]: an rpc's error is `RpcOnlyError` or an enum with exactly one `rpcFailure(RpcFailure)` case; `corpus.CartError` isn't
 --> src/corpus/failure-case-with-wrong-payload.k:7:22
  |
2 | enum CartError implements Error, Codable {
  |      --------- declared here
7 |     rpc add() throws CartError -> Int
  |                      ^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Add exactly one `case rpcFailure(RpcFailure)` to the error enum.

### K5503 `rpc-payload-not-codable`

**Error.** Rpc parameters, results and errors must be `Codable`.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/protocols/secret-param.k`):

```k,ignore
// `Secret<T>` is not `Codable`, so it can't be an rpc parameter.
import k.rpc.RpcOnlyError

protocol Accounts {
    rpc rotate(key: Secret<String>) throws RpcOnlyError
}
```

```text
error[K5503]: an rpc parameter crosses the wire, so it must be `Codable`; `Secret<String>` isn't
 --> src/corpus/secret-param.k:5:21
  |
5 |     rpc rotate(key: Secret<String>) throws RpcOnlyError
  |                     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Make the type `Codable`.

### K5504 `rpc-implementation-not-server`

**Error.** A protocol is implemented only by a server-side service.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/protocols/struct-implements-protocol.k`):

```k,ignore
// Protocols are implemented by services only, which are server-only.
import k.rpc.RpcOnlyError

protocol Ping {
    rpc ping() throws RpcOnlyError
}

struct LocalPing implements Ping {
    rpc ping() async throws RpcOnlyError {
    }
}
```

```text
error[K5504]: a protocol is implemented by a service, which runs on the server
 --> src/corpus/struct-implements-protocol.k:8:29
  |
8 | struct LocalPing implements Ping {
  |                             ^^^^
```

**Fix:** Implement the protocol in a service that is server-side (it may inject repositories).

### K5505 `rpc-handler-mismatch`

**Error.** An rpc handler doesn't repeat its rpc's signature.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/protocols/handler-mismatch.k`):

```k,ignore
// Handlers repeat their rpc's signature, `throws` included; a missing handler is a missing member.
import k.rpc.RpcFailure
import k.rpc.RpcOnlyError

enum CartError implements Error, Codable {
    case empty
    case rpcFailure(RpcFailure)
}

protocol CartProtocol {
    rpc count() throws CartError -> Int
    rpc clear() throws RpcOnlyError
}

service CartApi implements CartProtocol {
    rpc count() async throws RpcOnlyError -> Int {
        return 0
    }

    rpc clear() async throws RpcOnlyError {
    }
}

protocol TagsProtocol {
    rpc list() throws RpcOnlyError -> List<String>
}

service TagsApi implements TagsProtocol {
}
```

```text
error[K5505]: `count` doesn't repeat the signature of `corpus.CartProtocol.count`
  --> src/corpus/handler-mismatch.k:16:9
   |
11 |     rpc count() throws CartError -> Int
   |         ----- declared here
16 |     rpc count() async throws RpcOnlyError -> Int {
   |         ^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Repeat the rpc's parameters, return type and `throws` in the handler.

### K5506 `handler-throws-rpc-failure`

**Error.** Only the runtime produces `rpcFailure`: a handler throws its error enum's own cases.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/protocols/handler-throws-rpc-failure.k`):

```k,ignore
// Only the runtime produces `rpcFailure` (28-rpc-wire-format.md): a handler
// that throws it is K5506 at the `throw`, however the case is written. Its
// own cases are fine, and so is client code passing `rpcFailure` on.
import k.rpc.RpcFailure

enum CartError implements Error, Codable {
    case outOfStock
    case rpcFailure(RpcFailure)
}

enum LookupError implements Error {
    case missing
    case rpcFailure(RpcFailure)
}

protocol CartProtocol {
    rpc add(id: Int) throws CartError -> Int
}

service CartApi implements CartProtocol {
    rpc add(id: Int) async throws CartError -> Int {
        if id < 0 {
            throw .rpcFailure(.offline)
        }
        if id == 0 {
            throw CartError.rpcFailure(.timeout)
        }
        throw CartError.outOfStock
    }
}

service CartClient {
    @Inject let api: CartProtocol

    func add(id: Int) async throws LookupError -> Int {
        do {
            return try await api.add(id: id)
        } catch .rpcFailure(let failure) {
            throw LookupError.rpcFailure(failure)
        } catch .outOfStock {
            throw .missing
        }
    }
}
```

```text
error[K5506]: only the runtime produces `rpcFailure`; a handler throws its own cases
  --> src/corpus/handler-throws-rpc-failure.k:23:13
   |
23 |             throw .rpcFailure(.offline)
   |             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

error[K5506]: only the runtime produces `rpcFailure`; a handler throws its own cases
  --> src/corpus/handler-throws-rpc-failure.k:26:13
   |
26 |             throw CartError.rpcFailure(.timeout)
   |             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Throw one of the error enum's own cases; `rpcFailure` is produced only by the runtime.

### K5507 `requires-on-handler`

**Error.** A `requires` clause on a service's rpc is never checked: the server runs the guards the protocol's rpc declares.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/protocols/requires-on-rpc-outside-a-protocol.k`):

```k,ignore
// Only a protocol's rpcs are served, so a `requires` clause on an rpc that no protocol declares
// guards nothing (K5507). There is no protocol rpc to move it to.
import k.auth.Authenticated
import k.rpc.RpcOnlyError

service Lone {
    rpc hello() async throws RpcOnlyError -> Bool requires Authenticated {
        return true
    }
}
```

```text
error[K5507]: the server never checks a `requires` clause on a handler; it runs the guards the protocol declares
 --> src/corpus/requires-on-rpc-outside-a-protocol.k:7:51
  |
7 |     rpc hello() async throws RpcOnlyError -> Bool requires Authenticated {
  |                                                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = help: only a protocol's rpcs are served: declare `hello` in a protocol that `Lone` implements, with the clause on its rpc
```

**Fix:** Move the clause to the protocol's rpc (the quick fix does it); for a library's protocol, check the caller in the handler instead.

## K6000–K6999: Persistence

### K6001 `untranslatable-query`

**Error.** A repository query lambda uses something that can't be translated to SQL.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/persistence/untranslatable-query.k`):

```k,ignore
// A query lambda that calls an arbitrary function can't be translated to SQL.
entity Note {
    @Id let id: Int
    var title: String
}

func isShort(title: String) -> Bool {
    return title.count < 10
}

repository NoteRepository for Note {
    func short() async -> List<Note> {
        return await notes.filter { note => isShort(title: note.title) }.list()
    }
}
```

```text
error[K6001]: a query lambda is translated to SQL, which can't call this function
  --> src/corpus/untranslatable-query.k:13:45
   |
13 |         return await notes.filter { note => isShort(title: note.title) }.list()
   |                                             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Use only fields, literals, parameters and the query operators the compiler translates; filter in K after loading if needed.

### K6002 `unsupported-column-type`

**Error.** An entity field has a type that can't be stored in a column.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/persistence/unsupported-column-types.k`):

```k,ignore
// Entity fields have column types; maps, plain structs and secrets are not.
struct Address {
    let city: String
}

entity Account {
    @Id let id: Int
    var settings: Map<String, String>
    var address: Address
    var token: Secret<String>
    var name: String
}
```

```text
error[K6002]: an entity column can't hold `Map<String, String>`
 --> src/corpus/unsupported-column-types.k:8:19
  |
8 |     var settings: Map<String, String>
  |                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

error[K6002]: an entity column can't hold `corpus.Address`
 --> src/corpus/unsupported-column-types.k:9:18
  |
9 |     var address: Address
  |                  ^^^^^^^

error[K6002]: an entity column can't hold `Secret<String>`
  --> src/corpus/unsupported-column-types.k:10:16
   |
10 |     var token: Secret<String>
   |                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Use a column type (`String`, `Int`, `Bool`, `Double`, `Decimal`, `Money`, `Date`, `Uuid`, an enum without payloads, …) or a `@Relation`.

### K6003 `reserved-table-prefix`

**Error.** An entity's table name starts with `k_`, which is reserved for the stdlib.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/persistence/reserved-table-prefix.k`):

```k,ignore
// The `k_` table prefix is reserved for the stdlib: `entity KCache` would be table `k_cache`.
entity KCache {
    @Id let id: Int
}

entity Cache {
    @Id let id: Int
}
```

```text
error[K6003]: `KCache` would be the table `k_cache`; the `k_` prefix is reserved
 --> src/corpus/reserved-table-prefix.k:2:8
  |
2 | entity KCache {
  |        ^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Rename the entity, or set another table name.

### K6004 `invalid-migration`

**Error.** A migration doesn't replay against the schema the earlier migrations leave.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/persistence/lock/migration-does-not-replay/`):

```k,ignore
// App.k
// A migration that names a missing table: K6004 at the call.
public app Demo {}
```

```k,ignore
// migrations/0001_create_notes.k
/// Creates `note`.
migration CreateNotes {
    func up(schema: Schema) {
        schema.createTable(name: "note") { table =>
            table.column(name: "id", type: .uuid).primaryKey(true)
            table.column(name: "title", type: .text)
            table.column(name: "status", type: .enumeration(cases: ["draft", "published"]))
        }
    }
}
```

```k,ignore
// migrations/0002_typo.k
/// Names a table that doesn't exist.
@Breaking("single instance")
migration Typo {
    func up(schema: Schema) {
        schema.alterTable(name: "notes") { table =>
            table.dropColumn(name: "title")
        }
    }
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/notes/Note.k
import k.crypto.Uuid

/// A note.
public entity Note {
    @Id let id: Uuid

    var title: String

    var status: NoteStatus = .draft
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/notes/NoteStatus.k
/// Where a note is in its life.
public enum NoteStatus {
    case draft
    case published
}
```

```text
error[K6004]: `0002_typo` doesn't replay: there is no table `notes` at this point of the migrations
 --> migrations/0002_typo.k:6:13
  |
6 |             table.dropColumn(name: "title")
  |             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Name only the tables, columns and cases the earlier migrations leave, with the schema builder's calls and literal arguments.

### K6005 `destructive-migration`

**Error.** A migration that drops a table or column, or renames or removes an enum case, needs `@Breaking("reason")`.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/persistence/lock/enum-case-removed-without-breaking/`):

```k,ignore
// App.k
// Removing a case rewrites stored values: K6005 without `@Breaking`.
public app Demo {}
```

```k,ignore
// migrations/0001_create_notes.k
/// Creates `note`.
migration CreateNotes {
    func up(schema: Schema) {
        schema.createTable(name: "note") { table =>
            table.column(name: "id", type: .uuid).primaryKey(true)
            table.column(name: "title", type: .text)
            table.column(name: "status", type: .enumeration(cases: ["draft", "published"]))
        }
    }
}
```

```k,ignore
// migrations/0002_remove_published.k
/// Drops publishing.
migration RemovePublished {
    func up(schema: Schema) {
        schema.alterTable(name: "note") { table =>
            table.removeEnumCase(column: "status", case: "published", replacement: "draft")
        }
    }
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/notes/Note.k
import k.crypto.Uuid

/// A note.
public entity Note {
    @Id let id: Uuid

    var title: String

    var status: NoteStatus = .draft
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/notes/NoteStatus.k
/// Where a note is in its life.
public enum NoteStatus {
    case draft
}
```

```text
error[K6005]: `0002_remove_published` removes the case `published` of `note.status` without `@Breaking`, which loses data
 --> migrations/0002_remove_published.k:5:13
  |
5 |             table.removeEnumCase(column: "status", case: "published", replacement: "draft")
  |             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = help: mark the migration `@Breaking("reason")`, saying why the loss is acceptable
```

**Fix:** Mark the migration `@Breaking("reason")`, saying why losing the data is acceptable.

### K6006 `live-schema-change`

**Error.** A migration drops or renames a table or column that no earlier migration retired; only `@Breaking("single instance")` allows it.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/persistence/lock/rename-live-column/`):

```k,ignore
// App.k
// A physical rename is a live change: K6006 without `@Breaking("single instance")`.
public app Demo {}
```

```k,ignore
// migrations/0001_create_notes.k
/// Creates `note`.
migration CreateNotes {
    func up(schema: Schema) {
        schema.createTable(name: "note") { table =>
            table.column(name: "id", type: .uuid).primaryKey(true)
            table.column(name: "title", type: .text)
            table.column(name: "status", type: .enumeration(cases: ["draft", "published"]))
        }
    }
}
```

```k,ignore
// migrations/0002_rename_title.k
/// Renames the column.
migration RenameTitle {
    func up(schema: Schema) {
        schema.alterTable(name: "note") { table =>
            table.renameColumn(from: "title", to: "heading")
        }
    }
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/notes/Note.k
import k.crypto.Uuid

/// A note.
public entity Note {
    @Id let id: Uuid

    var heading: String

    var status: NoteStatus = .draft
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/notes/NoteStatus.k
/// Where a note is in its life.
public enum NoteStatus {
    case draft
    case published
}
```

```text
error[K6006]: `0002_rename_title` renames the column `note.title`, which the previous release still reads during a rolling deploy
 --> migrations/0002_rename_title.k:5:13
  |
5 |             table.renameColumn(from: "title", to: "heading")
  |             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = help: rename across two releases instead (add the new column, backfill it and retire the old one; drop it later with `k migrate new --drop-retired`), or rename only the field and keep the column (`k migrate rename`); a single-instance app can mark the migration `@Breaking("single instance")`
```

**Fix:** Retire the table or column first and drop it in a later release (`k migrate new --drop-retired`); a single-instance app marks the migration `@Breaking("single instance")`.

## K7000–K7499: Forms and validation

### K7001 `form-value-outside-handle`

**Error.** `form.value` is readable only inside the action passed to `form.handle(...)`.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/forms/value-in-view.k`):

```k,ignore
// `value` can't be read in the view, where the fields may not parse.

import k.validation.Length
import k.validation.Validatable
import k.validation.ValidationError

struct SignupRequest implements Codable, Validatable {
    @Length(min: 3) var name: String
    var age: Int
    var newsletter: Bool = false
}

service Accounts {
    func signup(request: SignupRequest) async throws ValidationError {
    }
}

page Signup {
    @Form var signup: SignupRequest = .empty

    view {
        text { signup.value.name }
    }
}
```

```text
error[K7001]: `value` is read only inside the action passed to `handle(…)`, where every field parses
  --> src/corpus/value-in-view.k:22:23
   |
22 |         text { signup.value.name }
   |                       ^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Read `form.value` inside the action passed to `form.handle(…)`.

### K7002 `empty-outside-form`

**Error.** `.empty` and `.empty(...)` are valid only as a `@Form` initializer.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/forms/empty-outside-form.k`):

```k,ignore
import k.validation.NotBlank
import k.validation.Validatable

struct SignInRequest implements Codable, Validatable {
    @NotBlank var email: String
    @NotBlank var password: String
}

let blank: SignInRequest = .empty
```

```text
error[K7002]: `.empty` is valid only as a `@Form` field's initializer
 --> src/corpus/empty-outside-form.k:9:28
  |
9 | let blank: SignInRequest = .empty
  |                            ^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Use `.empty` only to initialize a `@Form` field.

### K7003 `format-on-string`

**Error.** `@Format(message:)` applies to fields of parsed types, not `String`.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/forms/format-on-optional-string.k`):

```k,ignore
// A `String?` can't fail to parse either.
import k.validation.Format
import k.validation.Validatable

struct Profile implements Validatable {
    @Format(message: "Enter a nickname") var nickname: String?
}
```

```text
error[K7003]: text always parses: `@Format` belongs on fields of parsed types
 --> src/corpus/format-on-optional-string.k:6:5
  |
6 |     @Format(message: "Enter a nickname") var nickname: String?
  |     ^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Use `@Matches` or `@Length` on a `String`, or change the field to the parsed type.

### K7004 `redundant-email`

**Warning.** `@Email` on an `EmailAddress` field is redundant; the type already validates.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/forms/redundant-email.k`):

```k,ignore
import k.text.EmailAddress
import k.validation.Email
import k.validation.Validatable

struct Contact implements Validatable {
    @Email var email: EmailAddress
    @Email var backup: String
}
```

```text
warning[K7004]: an `EmailAddress` validates itself; `@Email` is redundant
 --> src/corpus/redundant-email.k:6:5
  |
6 |     @Email var email: EmailAddress
  |     ^^^^^^
  |
  = fix: Remove `@Email`
```

**Fix:** Remove `@Email` (machine-applicable fix).

### K7005 `matches-not-literal`

**Error.** `@Matches` takes a string literal, so the pattern can be checked at compile time.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/forms/matches-not-literal.k`):

```k,ignore
// `@Matches` takes a string literal: no interpolation, no concatenation, no constants.
import k.validation.Matches
import k.validation.Validatable

let prefix = "ab"

struct Codes implements Validatable {
    @Matches("^{prefix}$") var interpolated: String
    @Matches("^a" + "b$") var joined: String
    @Matches(prefix) var named: String
}
```

```text
error[K7005]: `@Matches` takes a string literal, known at compile time
 --> src/corpus/matches-not-literal.k:8:14
  |
8 |     @Matches("^{prefix}$") var interpolated: String
  |              ^^^^^^^^^^^^

error[K7005]: `@Matches` takes a string literal, known at compile time
 --> src/corpus/matches-not-literal.k:9:14
  |
9 |     @Matches("^a" + "b$") var joined: String
  |              ^^^^^^^^^^^

error[K7005]: `@Matches` takes a string literal, known at compile time
  --> src/corpus/matches-not-literal.k:10:14
   |
10 |     @Matches(prefix) var named: String
   |              ^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Pass the pattern as a string literal.

### K7006 `invalid-regex`

**Error.** A `@Matches` pattern is not a valid regular expression.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/forms/matches-invalid-patterns.k`):

```k,ignore
// An invalid pattern is reported at its string literal.
import k.validation.Matches
import k.validation.Validatable

struct Codes implements Validatable {
    @Matches("(ab") var open: String
    @Matches("*a") var star: String
    @Matches("a{{2,1}") var range: String
    @Matches("^ok$") var fine: String
}
```

```text
error[K7006]: invalid regular expression: unterminated group
 --> src/corpus/matches-invalid-patterns.k:6:14
  |
6 |     @Matches("(ab") var open: String
  |              ^^^^^

error[K7006]: invalid regular expression: nothing to repeat
 --> src/corpus/matches-invalid-patterns.k:7:14
  |
7 |     @Matches("*a") var star: String
  |              ^^^^

error[K7006]: invalid regular expression: numbers out of order in a `{}` quantifier
 --> src/corpus/matches-invalid-patterns.k:8:14
  |
8 |     @Matches("a{{2,1}") var range: String
  |              ^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Correct the regular expression.

## K7500–K7999: Tests

### K7501 `expect-not-bool`

**Error.** `expect` takes a `Bool` condition.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/tests/expect-not-bool.k`):

```k,ignore
// path: src/corpus/Math.test.k
test "adds" {
    expect 1 + 1 == 2
    expect 1 + 1
}
```

```text
error[K7501]: `expect` takes a `Bool`, found `Int`
 --> src/corpus/Math.test.k:4:12
  |
4 |     expect 1 + 1
  |            ^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Pass a `Bool` expression to `expect`.

### K7502 `expect-throws-cannot-throw`

**Error.** The block of `expect throws E { … }` can't throw `E`.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/tests/expect-throws-cannot-throw.k`):

```k,ignore
// path: src/corpus/Weather.test.k
// The block of `expect throws E` must be able to throw `E`.
enum WeatherError implements Error {
    case unknownPlace
}

enum OtherError implements Error {
    case broken
}

func degrees() -> Int {
    return 20
}

func forecast(place: String) async throws WeatherError -> Int {
    throw WeatherError.unknownPlace
}

test Weather {
    test "cannot throw at all" {
        expect throws WeatherError.unknownPlace {
            let value = degrees()
        }
    }

    test "throws another type" {
        expect throws OtherError.broken {
            try await forecast(place: "Nowhere")
        }
    }
}
```

```text
error[K7502]: this block can't throw the expected error
  --> src/corpus/Weather.test.k:21:9
   |
21 |         expect throws WeatherError.unknownPlace {
   |         ^^^^^^

error[K7502]: this block can't throw the expected error
  --> src/corpus/Weather.test.k:27:9
   |
27 |         expect throws OtherError.broken {
   |         ^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Put a call that can throw that error inside the block, or expect another error.

### K7503 `unbound-test-config`

**Error.** A test group's dependency graph reaches an app config that no `use` rule binds.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/tests/unbound-config/`):

```k,ignore
// src/mail/MailConfig.k
// An app config.
public config MailConfig {
    @Env("SMTP_HOST") let host: String
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/mail/Mailer.k
// A service that needs it.
public service Mailer {
    @Inject let config: MailConfig
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/mail/Mailer.test.k
// Tests never read the environment: a group whose graph reaches an app config binds it.
test Unbound {
    @Inject let mailer: Mailer

    test "runs" {
        expect true
    }
}

test Bound {
    use MailConfig(host: "localhost") for MailConfig

    @Inject let mailer: Mailer

    test "runs" {
        expect true
    }
}
```

```text
error[K7503]: tests never read the environment: bind `MailConfig` with `use … for MailConfig`
 --> src/mail/Mailer.test.k:2:6
  |
2 | test Unbound {
  |      ^^^^^^^
  |
  = note: Unbound → Mailer → MailConfig
```

**Fix:** Bind the config in the test group: `use SomeConfig.sample for SomeConfig`.

### K7510 `test-failed`

**Error.** A test failed when `k test` or `k check` ran it.

**Fix:** Fix the code or the expectation; the notes show the value of each part of the failed expression.

## K8000–K8999: Lockfiles, manifest and packages

### K8001 `breaking-change`

**Error.** A change breaks a lockfile's recorded contract without `@Breaking`.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/rpc/lock/protocol-no-longer-served/`):

```k,ignore
// App.k
public app Shop {}
```

```k,ignore
// src/cart/CartApi.k
/// The cart, served to the browser.
public protocol CartApi {
    /// Adds an item; answers the new count.
    rpc add(item: CartItem) throws CartError -> Int
    /// Empties the cart.
    rpc clear() throws CartError
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/cart/CartError.k
import k.rpc.RpcFailure

/// Why a cart call failed.
public enum CartError implements Error, Codable {
    /// The product is gone.
    case outOfStock
    /// The call failed outside the handler.
    case rpcFailure(RpcFailure)
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/cart/CartItem.k
/// One line of the cart.
public struct CartItem implements Codable {
    /// The product.
    let productId: Int
    /// How many.
    let quantity: Int
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/cart/CartService.k
/// No longer implements the protocol.
public service CartService {}
```

```text
error[K8001]: `cart.CartApi` is recorded in rpc.lock, but the app no longer serves it
 --> App.k:1:12
  |
1 | public app Shop {}
  |            ^^^^
  |
  = note: callers already deployed still call it; keep implementing it, or delete its entries from rpc.lock once none does
```

**Fix:** Undo the breaking change, or mark it deliberate with `@Breaking("reason")` once no deployed caller relies on the old shape.

### K8002 `invalid-lockfile`

**Error.** A lockfile can't be read.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/jobs/storage-lock-invalid/`):

```k,ignore
// An unreadable storage.lock is K8002 at the offending line.
import k.crypto.Uuid
import k.server.Job
import k.server.JobError

/// What the confirmation job needs.
struct OrderConfirmation implements Codable {
    let orderId: Uuid
}

/// Sends an order's confirmation.
service OrderConfirmationJob implements Job<OrderConfirmation> {
    func run(payload: OrderConfirmation) async throws JobError {
    }
}
```

```text
error[K8002]: storage.lock can't be read: unclosed table, expected `]`
 --> storage.lock:6:1
  |
6 | [jobs.order-confirmation
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

**Fix:** Restore the lockfile from version control, or fix its syntax.

### K8003 `incompatible-job-payload`

**Error.** A job's payload changed incompatibly with `storage.lock`; queued jobs couldn't be decoded.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/jobs/storage-lock-payload-field-type-changed/`):

```k,ignore
// A field of a recorded payload changed its type (K8003).
import k.crypto.Uuid
import k.server.Job
import k.server.JobError

/// What the confirmation job needs.
struct OrderConfirmation implements Codable {
    let orderId: Uuid
    let note: Int
}

/// Sends an order's confirmation.
service OrderConfirmationJob implements Job<OrderConfirmation> {
    func run(payload: OrderConfirmation) async throws JobError {
    }
}
```

```text
error[K8003]: the payload of job `order-confirmation` changed incompatibly with storage.lock; jobs queued by the previous release couldn't be decoded
  --> src/store/OrderConfirmationJob.k:13:45
   |
13 | service OrderConfirmationJob implements Job<OrderConfirmation> {
   |                                             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
   |
   = note: field `note` of `store.OrderConfirmation` changed type from `String` to `Int`
   = note: keep the recorded shape (only optional fields and new enum cases are compatible), or mark the job `@Breaking("reason")` once no such job can be queued
```

**Fix:** Keep the payload compatible (add optional fields only), or give the job a new `@JobName` and drain the old queue.

### K8004 `schema-drift`

**Error.** The entities differ from `schema.lock`; `k migrate new` writes the migration.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/persistence/lock/no-lock/`):

```k,ignore
// App.k
// An entity in an app without migrations or schema.lock: K8004, run `k migrate new`.
public app Demo {}
```

```k,ignore
// src/notes/Note.k
import k.crypto.Uuid

/// A note.
public entity Note {
    @Id let id: Uuid

    var title: String

    var status: NoteStatus = .draft
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/notes/NoteStatus.k
/// Where a note is in its life.
public enum NoteStatus {
    case draft
    case published
}
```

```text
error[K8004]: `notes.Note` has no table in schema.lock
 --> src/notes/Note.k:4:15
  |
4 | public entity Note {
  |               ^^^^
  |
  = help: run `k migrate new "description"`: it writes the migration and records it in schema.lock
```

**Fix:** Run `k migrate new "description"`; for a renamed entity or field, `k migrate rename old new` keeps its table or column.

### K8005 `schema-lock-mismatch`

**Error.** Replaying `migrations/` doesn't produce the schema `schema.lock` records.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/persistence/lock/lock-out-of-date/`):

```k,ignore
// App.k
// A migration whose change schema.lock doesn't record: K8005 at the lock's table.
public app Demo {}
```

```k,ignore
// migrations/0001_create_notes.k
/// Creates `note`.
migration CreateNotes {
    func up(schema: Schema) {
        schema.createTable(name: "note") { table =>
            table.column(name: "id", type: .uuid).primaryKey(true)
            table.column(name: "title", type: .text)
            table.column(name: "status", type: .enumeration(cases: ["draft", "published"]))
        }
    }
}
```

```k,ignore
// migrations/0002_add_body.k
/// Adds a body.
migration AddBody {
    func up(schema: Schema) {
        schema.alterTable(name: "note") { table =>
            table.addColumn(name: "body", type: .text).nullable(true)
        }
    }
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/notes/Note.k
import k.crypto.Uuid

/// A note.
public entity Note {
    @Id let id: Uuid

    var title: String

    var status: NoteStatus = .draft
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/notes/NoteStatus.k
/// Where a note is in its life.
public enum NoteStatus {
    case draft
    case published
}
```

```text
error[K8005]: schema.lock doesn't record the table `note` as the migrations leave it
 --> schema.lock:4:1
  |
4 | [tables.note]
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = note: the migrations create the column `body`, which schema.lock doesn't record
  = help: run `k build`, which records the schema the migrations produce in schema.lock, and review the change; if the lock was right, a migration changed after it was recorded
```

**Fix:** Run `k build` to record the schema the migrations produce in `schema.lock`, and review the change.

### K8006 `migration-order`

**Error.** A migration file's number doesn't match its position in `schema.lock`'s `migrations` list.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/persistence/lock/listed-migration-missing/`):

```k,ignore
// App.k
// The lock lists a migration whose file is gone: K8006 at the entry.
public app Demo {}
```

```k,ignore
// migrations/0001_create_notes.k
/// Creates `note`.
migration CreateNotes {
    func up(schema: Schema) {
        schema.createTable(name: "note") { table =>
            table.column(name: "id", type: .uuid).primaryKey(true)
            table.column(name: "title", type: .text)
            table.column(name: "status", type: .enumeration(cases: ["draft", "published"]))
        }
    }
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/notes/Note.k
import k.crypto.Uuid

/// A note.
public entity Note {
    @Id let id: Uuid

    var title: String

    var status: NoteStatus = .draft
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/notes/NoteStatus.k
/// Where a note is in its life.
public enum NoteStatus {
    case draft
    case published
}
```

```text
error[K8006]: schema.lock lists the migration `0002_lost`, but `migrations/0002_lost.k` doesn't exist
 --> schema.lock:2:36
  |
2 | migrations = ["0001_create_notes", "0002_lost"]
  |                                    ^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = help: restore the file: a migration is history, and databases that applied it expect it
```

**Fix:** Number each migration file by its position in `schema.lock`'s `migrations` list, and keep every listed file.

### K8007 `removed-url`

**Error.** A URL `routes.lock` records is no longer served, and no redirect keeps it working.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/routing/lock/removed-page/`):

```k,ignore
// App.k
// A removed page whose URL nothing serves and no redirect keeps: K8007 at the
// lock's entry.
public app Demo {
    metadata {
        title("Demo")
    }
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/site/About.k
/// The About page.
public page About at "/about" {
    view {
        paragraph { "About" }
    }
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/site/Health.k
import k.http.HttpResponse
import k.http.IncomingRequest

/// Answers load balancers.
public page Health at "/health" {
    @Get
    func check(request: IncomingRequest) async -> HttpResponse {
        return HttpResponse(status: .ok)
    }
}
```

```k,ignore
// src/site/Product.k
import k.crypto.Uuid

/// The Product page.
public page Product {
    @Param let id: Uuid

    view {
        paragraph { "Product" }
    }
}
```

```text
error[K8007]: `/pricing` (page `pricing`) is no longer served: `site.Pricing` was removed or renamed
 --> routes.lock:9:1
  |
9 | [pages.pricing]
  | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  |
  = help: keep the URL with `at "/pricing"`, add a redirect under `[redirects]` in routes.lock (`"/pricing" = "<page case>"`), or delete the entry once no link to it needs to work
```

**Fix:** Name the old URL with `at`, add a redirect under `[redirects]` in `routes.lock` (`k build` adds one for a renamed page), or delete the entry once nothing needs the URL.

### K8008 `incompatible-storage-key`

**Error.** A storage key changed incompatibly with `storage.lock`; stored values would no longer decode.

Example (`tests/corpus/sema/app/storage/case-removed/`):


**Fix:** Keep the key's name and value shape (add optional fields only), or mark the key `@Breaking("reason")` once its service handles `.unreadable`.

### K8101 `invalid-manifest`

**Error.** `k.toml` is malformed or lacks a required key.

**Fix:** Fix the syntax of `k.toml`, and give `[package]` its `name` and `k` keys.

### K8102 `unknown-dependency`

**Error.** A dependency can't be resolved: `{ workspace = true }` names no member of the workspace.

**Fix:** Name a member of the workspace, or add the member to the root `k.toml`'s `members`.

### K8103 `missing-workspace-member`

**Error.** A workspace member listed in `members` has no `k.toml`.

**Fix:** Create the member's `k.toml`, or remove it from `members`.

### K8104 `package-cycle`

**Error.** Packages depend on each other in a cycle; the dependency graph must be acyclic.

**Fix:** Move what both packages need into a library both depend on.

### K8105 `app-dependency`

**Error.** Only libraries can be depended on; an app can't be a dependency.

**Fix:** Depend on a library instead; move the shared code out of the app into one.

### K8106 `duplicate-module`

**Error.** Two packages of one build declare the same module.

**Fix:** Rename one of the modules.

## K9000–K9999: Driver, I/O and internal errors

### K9001 `invalid-utf8`

**Error.** A source file is not valid UTF-8.

**Fix:** Save the file as UTF-8.

### K9002 `io-error`

**Error.** A file or directory could not be read.

**Fix:** Check that the path exists and is readable.

### K9003 `tests-not-run`

**Error.** `k check` couldn't build or run the project's tests.

**Fix:** Run `k test` to see why the tests couldn't be built or run; the message names the cause. `--no-tests` checks without them.
